labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c

issue.body:
The async video lifecycle test polls every 20 ms, issuing one GET per pending job plus a liveness probe on every iteration. Each request also opens its own session, creating unnecessary HTTP traffic and access logs during GPU generation and intentional timeout waits.

Poll job status every 200 ms, probe liveness at most once per second within each wait, and reuse a test-scoped session for serial GETs. Concurrent POST submissions retain independent sessions. All 16 lifecycle assertions, the 90-second wait deadline, and the 10-second HTTP timeout stay unchanged.

Validation: pre-commit passed. A real HTTP regression using the actual test helpers reduced GETs from 180 to 18 and liveness probes from 60 to 2 for the same two-job completion window; serial GETs reused one TCP connection. Expected failures, unexpected terminal states, progress/status regressions and invalid completion progress remained covered. GPU lifecycle CI is pending.

issue.title: [Feat] multimodal: Add bounded GPU feature publication admission
issue.body:
## Summary

Add opt-in, bounded admission for CUDA IPC/VMM feature publication. Related to #43402; this does **not** fix its CUDA-driver hang or cap upstream decoder/preprocessing allocations.

- Reserve the whole publication batch atomically, accounting for alignment, fragmentation and IPC control slots. Wait without holding partial slices or occupying the copy worker.
- `--mm-admission-timeout-ms 0` rejects on pressure; positive values wait up to the deadline. Oversized batches return 413, temporary pressure 429. HTTP/OpenAI/SSE and Python/Rust gRPC preserve these errors.
- Publish asynchronously on an ordered copy stream. Retain original and contiguous/native tensor owners until device copy completion, including cancellation and failed dispatch. Do not allocate a contiguous copy before a failed reservation.
- Preserve ACK/generation semantics and VMM packing; expose pool, pending, lease-lifetime and reclamation diagnostics. Include VLM, server-argument and K3 usage documentation.

Unset preserves existing behavior. No default backend/transport change, additional HBM pool, or silent CPU fallback on the guarded path. PD/EPD is outside this opt-in implementation.

## Development validation

### Stream-context cleanup follow-up: `cede5e31`

Protect the whole CUDA stream context around guarded publication. Before publication starts, context construction/entry errors return reservations; after publication succeeds, context-exit errors cancel every returned proxy through the existing ready/ACK lifecycle. Pool-owned publication failures retain their own rollback, avoiding double release. Failed cancellation retains the poisoned lease instead of reusing memory while a copy may still be in flight. No new synchronization, scheduling fast path, backend policy or CPU fallback is introduced.

Exact-source validation on an isolated single B300 (driver 580.126.20) passed **740 CPU tests + 616 subtests**, **23 GPU tests + 4 subtests**, and **12 real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B Engine input/identity tests** across CPU, legacy IPC and guarded IPC with two processor workers. **15 cross-GPU VMM tests were skipped** because at least three GPUs are required; the single-device guarded VMM case ran. Final exits were zero and device usage returned to zero. The IPC producer-lifetime warning remains recorded.

The same tests on the previous production source reproduce both pre-publication context failures and both post-publication cleanup assertions; the existing copy-failure double-release guard passes both versions. Context errors are injected at the external API boundary around real allocator/copy/ACK/recycler operations, not a reproduction of a corrupted CUDA driver. Logs, native exit codes and source hashes are preserved and verified. This correctness fix does **not** resolve the performance gate, establish cross-mode bitwise output parity, or justify removing draft. New-head targeted CI is requested separately.

Test-only follow-up `416c35d1e84766897adc060ba72848e2f4e202ac` fixes abort-test expectations that read proxy fields after cleanup had cleared them. The tests now snapshot the original proxies before execution, assert the exact cancellation sequence, and assert both fields are cleared. Clean published parent `e2441d3` reproduced all three intended assertion failures; the fixed head passed both full related CPU files (**72 tests + 47 subtests**, zero failures/errors/skips) on isolated development hardware. Production source is unchanged; this does not resolve the performance gate. [Targeted CPU CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42897376154) passed on an explicitly verified checkout of `416c35d1`: 60 manager tests and 12 abort-cleanup cases, with no failures or skips. [Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42897173617) passed on synthetic merge `f507aa1e10`, which includes this head. No new GPU or Rust runtime result is claimed for this test-only follow-up.

Documentation-only follow-up `e2441d34764184647eb83490a2ba2fefeec4c143` clarifies cancellation, in-flight publication and safe pool reclamation. Runtime source is unchanged from `1a25c0a1`; all runtime and performance results below retain that tested-head attribution. Changed-file pre-commit, Mintlify build validation and internal link/anchor/redirect checks passed locally (Node 24.22.1, Mint 4.2.559). New-head Mintlify deployment and link checks passed. [Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42889365134) passed on synthetic merge `292faeb2c6` (including `e2441d3`), with pre-commit, offline references, all 67 cookbook checks and Mintlify links passing. No GPU rerun was requested for this paragraph; these docs checks do not resolve the performance gate.

### Updated validation: `1a25c0a104c5e2e799cf9b06412fae8d39903cf5`

Resolved the argument-field-order conflict with a normal merge of main `2d93fbfe`; existing argument positions and the admission option are preserved. The following checks ran against the exact merged source on an isolated single B300 (driver 580.126.20, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, torchvision 0.29.2, Transformers 5.19.0):

- 15 CPU test files: **739 tests + 614 subtests passed**.
- Complete CUDA IPC/VMM transport test files: **20 tests + 4 subtests passed**; **15 multi-GPU VMM cases skipped** because only one GPU was available. The real single-device guarded VMM case ran; this is not cross-device/FABRIC coverage.
- Real Qwen2.5-VL HF processor comparison: **60 calls, 48 exact comparisons passed**, covering worker modes, cache on/off, image order/duplicates and RGB/RGBA input.
- Four real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B Engine input/identity tests in each of CPU transport, legacy CUDA IPC and guarded CUDA IPC: **12 cases passed**, with two processor workers.
- Native `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p sglang-grpc --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and **19 `sglang-grpc` library tests passed**.

All exit markers were zero; logs and source/model provenance were preserved and SHA256-verified. An IPC producer-lifetime warning remains in the raw output, so these checks are not a leak-free soak claim.

**Keeping this PR draft:** the exact-head normal-serving replay completed, but concurrency-8 TTFT failed the performance gate (details below). These functional results do not establish performance acceptance, full K3/EPD/MNNVL validation, a physical decoder/preprocessing HBM cap, or a fix for the production CUDA driver hang. Feature-pool admission is the scope of this PR; the separate full-preprocessor budget work is not included. Targeted CI must be assessed on this exact head separately from older-head results.

### Previous head

Previous head `67d60e286f91de5004dd43b1fa95733b800d1f9b` preserves the `7a68600` ready-write regression and adds a processor-worker cancellation fix. The worker prepares request-owned tensors; legacy IPC leases are published only after the awaiting caller receives the result. Hashing and normal CPU-transport copies stay on the original worker. Default worker/backend policy is unchanged.

On isolated B300 (driver 595.91.07), this exact head passed 724 CPU-hidden tests + 600 subtests, 20 single-card transport tests + 4 subtests (15 unsupported cross-GPU cases skipped), 60 pinned-HF calls with 48 exact comparisons, and all four real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B input-format cases in each of CPU, legacy IPC and guarded IPC modes with two processor workers. All final exits were 0; GPU memory returned to zero. The old `7a68600` source reproduces the orphaned lease and worker-side publication assertions. One intermediate validation harness expected only one negative-control failure and stopped; that failed attempt is retained, and the final harness verifies both intended assertions without weakening the tests.

IPC producer-lifetime teardown warnings remain recorded. This is not a long soak or a new performance/full-K3/EPD/MNNVL result; legacy pool-miss D2H fallback remains part of publication and is not claimed to be off-loop.

Previous merge head `4af21ca298697bcccb9f830b018e99d7e2513332` normally merges pinned main `6d143e51b2a4`. The only manual conflict resolution preserves main's positional field order and appends the new admission argument afterward.

Exact-head isolated B300 validation passed 668 CPU-hidden tests + 580 subtests; 18 single-card IPC/VMM tests + 2 subtests; ordinary/streaming session equivalence and three abort/drain/flush/recovery waves with each of one and two tokenizer workers; Linux Rust Clippy and all 19 gRPC unit tests. Fifteen cross-GPU VMM tests require at least three GPUs and were skipped on the single-card development box, not counted as passes. All jobs exited 0 and GPU memory returned to zero. The IPC producer-lifetime teardown warning remains recorded.

The following broader development/performance evidence is from pre-merge production head `33b57e7c3bf48cc4595f07b93ca66812180e21bf`, on isolated NVIDIA B300 hardware; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, driver 580.126.20. It is not relabeled as a new-head performance replay.

- Nine CPU-hidden interface/configuration/cleanup/metrics files: 668 tests + 577 subtests passed.
- Five transport/configuration files: 132 passed; the explicit FABRIC test failed with `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED(800)`. This is missing coverage, not a green run. CUDA IPC and local POSIX VMM cases passed. An IPC producer-lifetime warning remains recorded at teardown.
- Negative controls on the earlier async candidate reproduce blocking publication and allocation before failed reservation. They do **not** directly reproduce a use-after-free or the production hang.
- Linux, repository-pinned Rust 1.92: workspace Clippy, multimodal Python/parallel Clippy, radix tch/doc-only Clippy, and all 19 gRPC unit tests passed. Other changed-file pre-commit checks passed; the macOS full-workspace build cannot compile existing Linux-only server APIs.
- Real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B, revision `66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3`: IPC normal serving, 413/429 pressure, gauge drain and correct recovery passed. Ten real-client disconnect waves also drained pool/pending gauges to zero. This is not a long soak.
- One and two tokenizer workers: ordinary/streaming sessions match independently salted full-history replay in output IDs and image-token counts; three 16-request abort/drain/flush/recovery waves per worker count passed. Pool budget is total across workers: an undersized two-worker configuration correctly returned 413. Successful lifecycle runs keep 16 MiB per worker (16/32 MiB total).

Prior-head `db2fb5d0` also passed Qwen3-VL-2B POSIX-VMM serving/abort/recovery, documentation checks and targeted FABRIC CI. Those results are retained as prior-head evidence, not relabeled as validation of this candidate.

## Performance — still draft

### Runtime-tested head `1a25c0a1`: completed, not accepted

On the same isolated B300 / pinned Qwen2.5-VL-3B revision and exact source above, compared admission unset versus 1000 ms. CUDA IPC, a sufficient **2 GiB pool in both arms**, default processor workers, preprocessing/radix caches off, CUDA graphs off, fixed 1024-square inputs and fixed histories; 32 conversations × 8 turns, repeat/append images, concurrency 1/8, three alternating pairs. All **6,144 measured + 1,536 multimodal warmup requests** completed with 16 actual output tokens. Timings, input hashes, prompt counts and zero cache hits were independently rechecked. Guarded CPU-spill counters stayed zero and publication gauges drained; legacy lacks these counters and is not reported as measured zero.

Paired-median change (guarded relative to legacy; positive latency is worse):

| Workload | Throughput | Hot p50 TTFT | Hot p95 TTFT | p95 E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Repeat, c1 | +1.02% | -1.64% | -1.46% | -0.99% |
| Repeat, c8 | +0.97% | **+13.52%** | +1.36% | +0.88% |
| Append, c1 | +1.10% | -0.95% | -0.54% | -3.61% |
| Append, c8 | -0.47% | **+8.22%** | -0.28% | -1.30% |

Repeat-c8 hot p50 regressed in **all three pairs: +12.59%, +13.52%, +15.83%**. Its third pair also lost 6.17% throughput with +13.87% hot p95 TTFT and +14.80% p95 E2E. Median throughput therefore does not establish acceptance or erase tail variation.

At c1, all 256 fixed inputs per scenario produced the same strings across all six runs. At c8, repeat/append had 15/9 variable inputs respectively; every observed cross-arm output set overlapped, with no stable arm-specific or disjoint output found in these three repeats. String equality nevertheless failed; this is not token/logit/embedding bitwise parity or proof that transport cannot affect correctness.

The original wrapper exited 0 and GPU memory returned to zero. The 2 GiB setting isolates normal-load admission overhead: it is **not a new recommended default**, a total preprocessing-memory cap, or a substitute for pressure/recovery tests. The 1 GiB preflight fit only five simultaneous maximum-size requests in this matrix. This result blocks draft promotion; the cause of the TTFT regression is not yet established.

### Earlier-head evidence

Same-commit admission-off/on replay; Qwen2.5-VL-3B, TP1, CUDA IPC, 64 MiB pool, preprocessing and radix caches off, CUDA graphs off, 448-square image, up to 8 output tokens.

The earlier `33b57e7` candidate's three-repeat c1/c8 matrix, with default and two processor workers, completed 6,144 measured requests with correct answers. Median throughput changes were -0.10%, +1.20%, -1.08%, +2.10%, respectively. However, default-worker c8 p95 E2E increased 33.1% in that shorter replay; this result remains recorded.

A longer, uninstrumented default-worker c8 replay used three alternating repetitions, 192 warmups and 1,024 measured requests per mode/repetition: all 6,144 measured requests passed.

| Metric | Admission off, median [range] | Admission on, median [range] |
|---|---:|---:|
| Requests/s | 80.883 [80.624–81.173] | 92.163 [88.933–95.857] |
| p95 E2E, ms | 104.205 [103.588–104.417] | 105.628 [104.213–107.834] |

This replay shows +13.95% median throughput and +1.37% median p95; it does not establish a universal speedup or explain away the earlier tail variability. The old public head's 9.53% default-worker / 3.73% two-worker throughput regressions are not substituted for candidate measurements.

Separate diagnostic timing found admission itself inexpensive (mean/p95 0.104/0.130 ms), while synchronous preprocessing delayed publication completion delivery on the event loop. Moving preprocessing to one off-loop worker reduced that delay but regressed end-to-end throughput in the diagnostic pair, so that experiment was **not** adopted. Instrumented timings are not pooled with the acceptance replay.

## Remaining gates

Keep draft. Runtime-tested head `1a25c0a1` CPU/IPC/VMM/H100 scoped tests and lint passed; this does not resolve performance acceptance. That source's c8 TTFT gate failed and remains unresolved. Broader workload/tail validation, full Kimi-K3/GLM, multi-node MNNVL/EPD and incident-shaped long soak are not established by these Qwen TP1 runs. No universal output/embedding bitwise-parity claim.

Native decoder memory accounting remains separate: a direct nvJPEG 13.0.1 hardware-decoder probe, without nvImageCodec, also bypassed a 16 MiB allocator-callback budget. An 8192-square JPEG increased observed device usage by 174.625 MiB with zero allocator callbacks (phase snapshots, not peak profiling). A hybrid-backend positive control did invoke and enforce the callback; changing backends would change decoded bytes. Publication admission cannot be advertised as a total preprocessing HBM cap or a complete OOM/hang fix.

## CI

Runtime-tested `1a25c0a1`: [CPU, 705 tests across ten files](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862006189), [5090 IPC, 14 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862032973), and [GB300 VMM, 21 tests including FABRIC/POSIX cross-GPU cases](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862058313) passed with exact source checkouts and no test skips. [Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42861386633) passed on PR merge `bb363157a2`. [H100 Qwen2.5-VL-7B serving](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862086005) passed all seven requested tests on the exact source: image-prefix reuse, mixed batch, single/multi-image, multi-turn, video and video+image. Its launch uses the existing default admission policy, so it is not a guarded-pressure test. Rust workspace runtime/build jobs were skipped on this follow-up; the isolated native checks above remain the runtime evidence. Exact-source documentation build and broken-link checks passed. The IPC producer-lifetime warning is retained; no leak-free soak or two-node validation claim.

Previous `67d60e2` passed [CPU, 54 tests across three files](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42732007085), [5090 IPC, 14 tests including worker cancellation and ready-write failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42732022452), [H100 Qwen input-format serving, 4 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42732038121), and [lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42731911330). All three test logs confirm checkout `67d60e286f91de5004dd43b1fa95733b800d1f9b`. The IPC producer-lifetime teardown warning remains recorded. Native/Rust change-detection workflows finished but skipped their runtime/build jobs on this follow-up; they are not counted as new Rust validation. This scoped result does not remove the remaining draft gates.

Pre-merge `33b57e7` scoped CI passed: [CPU, 668 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690843241), [IPC, 12 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690864250), [GB300 VMM, 21 tests including FABRIC round-trip/recycling](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690885872), and [MRoPE session serving](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690908210). This resolves that head's scoped FABRIC coverage gap, not full-model/multi-node validation.

Previous head `4af21ca` passed [CPU, 668 tests across nine files](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42696598137), [IPC, 12 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42696620111), [GB300 VMM, 21 tests including FABRIC round-trip/recycling](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42696642714), [MRoPE session serving](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42696679329), [Rust workspace](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42696527285), and [lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42696374742). Test checkout SHAs were verified. Automatic draft/opt-in gate failures do not mean the affected runtime tests executed; this is not a claim of full CI or merge readiness. No full unrelated CI matrix was requested.

The worker prepares request-owned tensors; legacy IPC leases are published only after the awaiting caller receives the result. Hashing and normal CPU-transport copies stay on the original worker. Default worker/backend policy is unchanged.

On isolated B300 (driver 595.91.07), this exact head passed 724 CPU-hidden tests + 600 subtests, 20 single-card transport tests + 4 subtests (15 unsupported cross-GPU cases skipped), 60 pinned-HF calls with 48 exact comparisons, and all four real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B input-format cases in each of CPU, legacy IPC and guarded IPC modes with two processor workers. All final exits were 0; GPU memory returned to zero. The old `7a68600` source reproduces the orphaned lease and worker-side publication assertions. One intermediate validation harness expected only one negative-control failure and stopped; that failed attempt is retained, and the final harness verifies both intended assertions without weakening the tests.

IPC producer-lifetime teardown warnings remain recorded. This is not a long soak or a new performance/full-K3/EPD/MNNVL result; legacy pool-miss D2H fallback remains part of publication and is not claimed to be off-loop.

Previous merge head `4af21ca298697bcccb9f830b018e99d7e2513332` normally merges pinned main `6d143e51b2a4`. The only manual conflict resolution preserves main's positional field order and appends the new admission argument afterward.

Exact-head isolated B300 validation passed 668 CPU-hidden tests + 580 subtests; 18 single-card IPC/VMM tests + 2 subtests; ordinary/streaming session equivalence and three abort/drain/flush/recovery waves with each of one and two tokenizer workers; Linux Rust Clippy and all 19 gRPC unit tests. Fifteen cross-GPU VMM tests require at least three GPUs and were skipped on the single-card development box, not counted as passes. All jobs exited 0 and GPU memory returned to zero. The IPC producer-lifetime teardown warning remains recorded.

The following broader development/performance evidence is from pre-merge production head `33b57e7c3bf48cc4595f07b93ca66812180e21bf`, on isolated NVIDIA B300 hardware; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, driver 580.126.20. It is not relabeled as a new-head performance replay.

- Nine CPU-hidden interface/configuration/cleanup/metrics files: 668 tests + 577 subtests passed.
- Five transport/configuration files: 132 passed; the explicit FABRIC test failed with `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED(800)`. This is missing coverage, not a green run. CUDA IPC and local POSIX VMM cases passed. An IPC producer-lifetime warning remains recorded at teardown.
- Negative controls on the earlier async candidate reproduce blocking publication and allocation before failed reservation. They do **not** directly reproduce a use-after-free or the production hang.
- Linux, repository-pinned Rust 1.92: workspace Clippy, multimodal Python/parallel Clippy, radix tch/doc-only Clippy, and all 19 gRPC unit tests passed. Other changed-file pre-commit checks passed; the macOS full-workspace build cannot compile existing Linux-only server APIs.
- Real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B, revision `66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3`: IPC normal serving, 413/429 pressure, gauge drain and correct recovery passed. Ten real-client disconnect waves also drained pool/pending gauges to zero. This is not a long soak.
- One and two tokenizer workers: ordinary/streaming sessions match independently salted full-history replay in output IDs and image-token counts; three 16-request abort/drain/flush/recovery waves per worker count passed. Pool budget is total across workers: an undersized two-worker configuration correctly returned 413. Successful lifecycle runs keep 16 MiB per worker (16/32 MiB total).

Prior-head `db2fb5d0` also passed Qwen3-VL-2B POSIX-VMM serving/abort/recovery, documentation checks and targeted FABRIC CI. Those results are retained as prior-head evidence, not relabeled as validation of this candidate.

## Performance — still draft

### Runtime-tested head `1a25c0a1`: completed, not accepted

On the same isolated B300 / pinned Qwen2.5-VL-3B revision and exact source above, compared admission unset versus 1000 ms. CUDA IPC, a sufficient **2 GiB pool in both arms**, default processor workers, preprocessing/radix caches off, CUDA graphs off, fixed 1024-square inputs and fixed histories; 32 conversations × 8 turns, repeat/append images, concurrency 1/8, three alternating pairs. All **6,144 measured + 1,536 multimodal warmup requests** completed with 16 actual output tokens. Timings, input hashes, prompt counts and zero cache hits were independently rechecked. Guarded CPU-spill counters stayed zero and publication gauges drained; legacy lacks these counters and is not reported as measured zero.

Paired-median change (guarded relative to legacy; positive latency is worse):

| Workload | Throughput | Hot p50 TTFT | Hot p95 TTFT | p95 E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Repeat, c1 | +1.02% | -1.64% | -1.46% | -0.99% |
| Repeat, c8 | +0.97% | **+13.52%** | +1.36% | +0.88% |
| Append, c1 | +1.10% | -0.95% | -0.54% | -3.61% |
| Append, c8 | -0.47% | **+8.22%** | -0.28% | -1.30% |

Repeat-c8 hot p50 regressed in **all three pairs: +12.59%, +13.52%, +15.83%**. Its third pair also lost 6.17% throughput with +13.87% hot p95 TTFT and +14.80% p95 E2E. Median throughput therefore does not establish acceptance or erase tail variation.

At c1, all 256 fixed inputs per scenario produced the same strings across all six runs. At c8, repeat/append had 15/9 variable inputs respectively; every observed cross-arm output set overlapped, with no stable arm-specific or disjoint output found in these three repeats. String equality nevertheless failed; this is not token/logit/embedding bitwise parity or proof that transport cannot affect correctness.

The original wrapper exited 0 and GPU memory returned to zero. The 2 GiB setting isolates normal-load admission overhead: it is **not a new recommended default**, a total preprocessing-memory cap, or a substitute for pressure/recovery tests. The 1 GiB preflight fit only five simultaneous maximum-size requests in this matrix. This result blocks draft promotion; the cause of the TTFT regression is not yet established.

### Earlier-head evidence

Same-commit admission-off/on replay; Qwen2.5-VL-3B, TP1, CUDA IPC, 64 MiB pool, preprocessing and radix caches off, CUDA graphs off, 448-square image, up to 8 output tokens.

The earlier `33b57e7` candidate's three-repeat c1/c8 matrix, with default and two processor workers, completed 6,144 measured requests with correct answers. Median throughput changes were -0.10%, +1.20%, -1.08%, +2.10%, respectively. However, default-worker c8 p95 E2E increased 33.1% in that shorter replay; this result remains recorded.

A longer, uninstrumented default-worker c8 replay used three alternating repetitions, 192 warmups and 1,024 measured requests per mode/repetition: all 6,144 measured requests passed.

| Metric | Admission off, median [range] | Admission on, median [range] |
|---|---:|---:|
| Requests/s | 80.883 [80.624–81.173] | 92.163 [88.933–95.857] |
| p95 E2E, ms | 104.205 [103.588–104.417] | 105.628 [104.213–107.834] |

This replay shows +13.95% median throughput and +1.37% median p95; it does not establish a universal speedup or explain away the earlier tail variability. The old public head's 9.53% default-worker / 3.73% two-worker throughput regressions are not substituted for candidate measurements.

Separate diagnostic timing found admission itself inexpensive (mean/p95 0.104/0.130 ms), while synchronous preprocessing delayed publication completion delivery on the event loop. Moving preprocessing to one off-loop worker reduced that delay but regressed end-to-end throughput in the diagnostic pair, so that experiment was **not** adopted. Instrumented timings are not pooled with the acceptance replay.

## Remaining gates

Keep draft. Runtime-tested head `1a25c0a1` CPU/IPC/VMM/H100 scoped tests and lint passed; this does not resolve performance acceptance. That source's c8 TTFT gate failed and remains unresolved. Broader workload/tail validation, full Kimi-K3/GLM, multi-node MNNVL/EPD and incident-shaped long soak are not established by these Qwen TP1 runs. No universal output/embedding bitwise-parity claim.

Native decoder memory accounting remains separate: a direct nvJPEG 13.0.1 hardware-decoder probe, without nvImageCodec, also bypassed a 16 MiB allocator-callback budget. An 8192-square JPEG increased observed device usage by 174.625 MiB with zero allocator callbacks (phase snapshots, not peak profiling). A hybrid-backend positive control did invoke and enforce the callback; changing backends would change decoded bytes. Publication admission cannot be advertised as a total preprocessing HBM cap or a complete OOM/hang fix.

## CI

Runtime-tested `1a25c0a1`: [CPU, 705 tests across ten files](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862006189), [5090 IPC, 14 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862032973), and [GB300 VMM, 21 tests including FABRIC/POSIX cross-GPU cases](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862058313) passed with exact source checkouts and no test skips. [Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42861386633) passed on PR merge `bb363157a2`. [H100 Qwen2.5-VL-7B serving](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862086005) passed all seven requested tests on the exact source: image-prefix reuse, mixed batch, single/multi-image, multi-turn, video and video+image. Its launch uses the existing default admission policy, so it is not a guarded-pressure test. Rust workspace runtime/build jobs were skipped on this follow-up; the isolated native checks above remain the runtime evidence. Exact-source documentation build and broken-link checks passed. The IPC producer-lifetime warning is retained; no leak-free soak or two-node validation claim.

Previous `67d60e2` passed [CPU, 54 tests across three files](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42732007085), [5090 IPC, 14 tests including worker cancellation and ready-write failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42732022452), [H100 Qwen input-format serving, 4 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42732038121), and [lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42731911330). All three test logs confirm checkout `67d60e286f91de5004dd43b1fa95733b800d1f9b`. The IPC producer-lifetime teardown warning remains recorded. Native/Rust change-detection workflows finished but skipped their runtime/build jobs on this follow-up; they are not counted as new Rust validation. This scoped result does not remove the remaining draft gates.

Pre-merge `33b57e7` scoped CI passed: [CPU, 668 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690843241), [IPC, 12 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690864250), [GB300 VMM, 21 tests including FABRIC round-trip/recycling](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690885872), and [MRoPE session serving](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690908210). This resolves that head's scoped FABRIC coverage gap, not full-model/multi-node validation.

issue.title: [CI] jit-kernel: B200 runs time out on a cold JIT cache after shared-header changes
issue.body:
[by Claude Code]

## Summary

When a commit changes a widely included JIT header, each B200 runner slot recompiles every JIT kernel from scratch on its next `jit-kernel-unit-test-4-gpu-b200` job. Those cold jobs take 48–61 min against the `Run test` step's 60-minute timeout (`.github/workflows/pr-test-jit-kernel.yml`), so whether a cold run fails is mostly luck. #42752 tracks one such failure as I58. This issue collects the evidence so the CI owners can choose a fix.

## Evidence

Commit `ff762d62f8` (#48942, "Unify FP32 activation functions in `sgl_kernel/activation.cuh`") merged at 2026-11-09 08:24 UTC. Durations of `jit-kernel-unit-test-4-gpu-b200` in `pr-test.yml` runs afterwards:

| Runner slot | First run after the change | Next run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `b200-cirrascale2` | 08:28, **61 min** | 09:41, 26 min |
| `b200-fin03-4-4567` | 08:47, **48 min** | — |
| `b200-cirrascale4-4567` | 09:10, **61 min, timed out** ([I58](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42591189061/job/129073246725)) | 11:07, 24 min |
| `b200-cirrascale1-0123` | 09:15, **60 min** | 12:07, 23 min |
| `b200-cirrascale4-0123` | 09:21, **58 min** | 11:45, 23 min |
| `b200-di01-0123` | 09:29, **59 min, cancelled** | 10:43, 25 min |
| `b200-fin03-4-0123` | 09:46, **48 min** | 11:17, 22 min |
| `b200-di01-4567` | 10:43, **61 min** (more than 2 h after the change) | 12:21, 25 min |

Before the change, the job took 23–27 min. In the timed-out run, all 109 test files that finished passed. Unrelated files slowed down the most: `test_compressed_tensors_fp4_numeric.py` went from about 12 s to 576–588 s.

## What the data shows

- **Every slot is cold once,** on its first job after the change, however long after the change that is. `di01-4567` was still cold more than 2 h later because it hadn't had a job yet. A rarely used slot can stay cold much longer.
- **The two slots on one host warm separately** (`-0123` and `-4567`), so each slot appears to keep its own cache.
- **Cold runs sit right at the limit.** Only one of the eight timed out, but five took 58–61 min.
- **It recurs** with every change that invalidates the cache: other shared JIT headers, toolchain or FlashInfer bumps. The PR that makes the change also runs cold in its own CI.

I only checked this one job, in `pr-test.yml` runs. The other jit-kernel jobs (1-GPU, H100) likely behave the same way.

## Options

| Option | Change | Trade-off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A. More headroom | Raise the `Run test` timeout (for example to 90 min) | One line, and it turns these failures into slow passes. But a run that really hangs then holds a B200 slot longer. |
| B. Warm the caches | After a merge that touches JIT headers (or bumps the toolchain), run a compile-only warmup on each B200 slot | Removes the cold runs from PRs. Needs a way to reach every slot, and costs runner time. |
| C. Share the cache | One cache per host, or a shared store, instead of one per slot | Halves the number of cold runs at least. Needs safe concurrent writes. |
| D. Report it | Log cache hit and miss counts per job, or flag runs that recompile | Makes these failures easy to recognize, but doesn't prevent them. |

A is the quick fix. B or C would address the cause.

Found while working through CI flakes from #42752.

issue.title: [Feat] multimodal: Add bounded GPU feature publication admission
issue.body:
## Summary

Add opt-in, bounded admission for CUDA IPC/VMM feature publication. Related to #43402; this does **not** fix its CUDA-driver hang or cap upstream decoder/preprocessing allocations.

- Reserve the whole publication batch atomically, accounting for alignment, fragmentation and IPC control slots. Wait without holding partial slices or occupying the copy worker.
- `--mm-admission-timeout-ms 0` rejects on pressure; positive values wait up to the deadline. Oversized batches return 413, temporary pressure 429. HTTP/OpenAI/SSE and Python/Rust gRPC preserve these errors.
- Publish asynchronously on an ordered copy stream. Retain original and contiguous/native tensor owners until device copy completion, including cancellation and failed dispatch. Do not allocate a contiguous copy before a failed reservation.
- Preserve ACK/generation semantics and VMM packing; expose pool, pending, lease-lifetime and reclamation diagnostics. Include VLM, server-argument and K3 usage documentation.

Unset preserves existing behavior. No default backend/transport change, additional HBM pool, or silent CPU fallback on the guarded path. PD/EPD is outside this opt-in implementation.

## Development validation

### Stream-context cleanup follow-up: `cede5e31`

Protect the whole CUDA stream context around guarded publication. Before publication starts, context construction/entry errors return reservations; after publication succeeds, context-exit errors cancel every returned proxy through the existing ready/ACK lifecycle. Pool-owned publication failures retain their own rollback, avoiding double release. Failed cancellation retains the poisoned lease instead of reusing memory while a copy may still be in flight. No new synchronization, scheduling fast path, backend policy or CPU fallback is introduced.

Exact-source validation on an isolated single B300 (driver 580.126.20) passed **740 CPU tests + 616 subtests**, **23 GPU tests + 4 subtests**, and **12 real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B Engine input/identity tests** across CPU, legacy IPC and guarded IPC with two processor workers. **15 cross-GPU VMM tests were skipped** because at least three GPUs are required; the single-device guarded VMM case ran. Final exits were zero and device usage returned to zero. The IPC producer-lifetime warning remains recorded.

The same tests on the previous production source reproduce both pre-publication context failures and both post-publication cleanup assertions; the existing copy-failure double-release guard passes both versions. Context errors are injected at the external API boundary around real allocator/copy/ACK/recycler operations, not a reproduction of a corrupted CUDA driver. Logs, native exit codes and source hashes are preserved and verified. This correctness fix does **not** resolve the performance gate, establish cross-mode bitwise output parity, or justify removing draft. New-head targeted CI is requested separately.

Test-only follow-up `416c35d1e84766897adc060ba72848e2f4e202ac` fixes abort-test expectations that read proxy fields after cleanup had cleared them. The tests now snapshot the original proxies before execution, assert the exact cancellation sequence, and assert both fields are cleared. Clean published parent `e2441d3` reproduced all three intended assertion failures; the fixed head passed both full related CPU files (**72 tests + 47 subtests**, zero failures/errors/skips) on isolated development hardware. Production source is unchanged; this does not resolve the performance gate. [Targeted CPU CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42897376154) passed on an explicitly verified checkout of `416c35d1`: 60 manager tests and 12 abort-cleanup cases, with no failures or skips. [Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42897173617) passed on synthetic merge `f507aa1e10`, which includes this head. No new GPU or Rust runtime result is claimed for this test-only follow-up.

Documentation-only follow-up `e2441d34764184647eb83490a2ba2fefeec4c143` clarifies cancellation, in-flight publication and safe pool reclamation. Runtime source is unchanged from `1a25c0a1`; all runtime and performance results below retain that tested-head attribution. Changed-file pre-commit, Mintlify build validation and internal link/anchor/redirect checks passed locally (Node 24.22.1, Mint 4.2.559). New-head Mintlify deployment and link checks passed. [Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42889365134) passed on synthetic merge `292faeb2c6` (including `e2441d3`), with pre-commit, offline references, all 67 cookbook checks and Mintlify links passing. No GPU rerun was requested for this paragraph; these docs checks do not resolve the performance gate.

### Updated validation: `1a25c0a104c5e2e799cf9b06412fae8d39903cf5`

Resolved the argument-field-order conflict with a normal merge of main `2d93fbfe`; existing argument positions and the admission option are preserved. The following checks ran against the exact merged source on an isolated single B300 (driver 580.126.20, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, torchvision 0.29.2, Transformers 5.19.0):

- 15 CPU test files: **739 tests + 614 subtests passed**.
- Complete CUDA IPC/VMM transport test files: **20 tests + 4 subtests passed**; **15 multi-GPU VMM cases skipped** because only one GPU was available. The real single-device guarded VMM case ran; this is not cross-device/FABRIC coverage.
- Real Qwen2.5-VL HF processor comparison: **60 calls, 48 exact comparisons passed**, covering worker modes, cache on/off, image order/duplicates and RGB/RGBA input.
- Four real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B Engine input/identity tests in each of CPU transport, legacy CUDA IPC and guarded CUDA IPC: **12 cases passed**, with two processor workers.
- Native `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p sglang-grpc --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and **19 `sglang-grpc` library tests passed**.

All exit markers were zero; logs and source/model provenance were preserved and SHA256-verified. An IPC producer-lifetime warning remains in the raw output, so these checks are not a leak-free soak claim.

**Keeping this PR draft:** the exact-head normal-serving replay completed, but concurrency-8 TTFT failed the performance gate (details below). These functional results do not establish performance acceptance, full K3/EPD/MNNVL validation, a physical decoder/preprocessing HBM cap, or a fix for the production CUDA driver hang. Feature-pool admission is the scope of this PR; the separate full-preprocessor budget work is not included. Targeted CI must be assessed on this exact head separately from older-head results.

### Previous head

Previous head `67d60e286f91de5004dd43b1fa95733b800d1f9b` preserves the `7a68600` ready-write regression and adds a processor-worker cancellation fix. The worker prepares request-owned tensors; legacy IPC leases are published only after the awaiting caller receives the result. Hashing and normal CPU-transport copies stay on the original worker. Default worker/backend policy is unchanged.

On isolated B300 (driver 595.91.07), this exact head passed 724 CPU-hidden tests + 600 subtests, 20 single-card transport tests + 4 subtests (15 unsupported cross-GPU cases skipped), 60 pinned-HF calls with 48 exact comparisons, and all four real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B input-format cases in each of CPU, legacy IPC and guarded IPC modes with two processor workers. All final exits were 0; GPU memory returned to zero. The old `7a68600` source reproduces the orphaned lease and worker-side publication assertions. One intermediate validation harness expected only one negative-control failure and stopped; that failed attempt is retained, and the final harness verifies both intended assertions without weakening the tests.

IPC producer-lifetime teardown warnings remain recorded. This is not a long soak or a new performance/full-K3/EPD/MNNVL result; legacy pool-miss D2H fallback remains part of publication and is not claimed to be off-loop.

Previous merge head `4af21ca298697bcccb9f830b018e99d7e2513332` normally merges pinned main `6d143e51b2a4`. The only manual conflict resolution preserves main's positional field order and appends the new admission argument afterward.

Exact-head isolated B300 validation passed 668 CPU-hidden tests + 580 subtests; 18 single-card IPC/VMM tests + 2 subtests; ordinary/streaming session equivalence and three abort/drain/flush/recovery waves with each of one and two tokenizer workers; Linux Rust Clippy and all 19 gRPC unit tests. Fifteen cross-GPU VMM tests require at least three GPUs and were skipped on the single-card development box, not counted as passes. All jobs exited 0 and GPU memory returned to zero. The IPC producer-lifetime teardown warning remains recorded.

The following broader development/performance evidence is from pre-merge production head `33b57e7c3bf48cc4595f07b93ca66812180e21bf`, on isolated NVIDIA B300 hardware; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, driver 580.126.20. It is not relabeled as a new-head performance replay.

- Nine CPU-hidden interface/configuration/cleanup/metrics files: 668 tests + 577 subtests passed.
- Five transport/configuration files: 132 passed; the explicit FABRIC test failed with `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED(800)`. This is missing coverage, not a green run. CUDA IPC and local POSIX VMM cases passed. An IPC producer-lifetime warning remains recorded at teardown.
- Negative controls on the earlier async candidate reproduce blocking publication and allocation before failed reservation. They do **not** directly reproduce a use-after-free or the production hang.
- Linux, repository-pinned Rust 1.92: workspace Clippy, multimodal Python/parallel Clippy, radix tch/doc-only Clippy, and all 19 gRPC unit tests passed. Other changed-file pre-commit checks passed; the macOS full-workspace build cannot compile existing Linux-only server APIs.
- Real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B, revision `66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3`: IPC normal serving, 413/429 pressure, gauge drain and correct recovery passed. Ten real-client disconnect waves also drained pool/pending gauges to zero. This is not a long soak.
- One and two tokenizer workers: ordinary/streaming sessions match independently salted full-history replay in output IDs and image-token counts; three 16-request abort/drain/flush/recovery waves per worker count passed. Pool budget is total across workers: an undersized two-worker configuration correctly returned 413. Successful lifecycle runs keep 16 MiB per worker (16/32 MiB total).

Prior-head `db2fb5d0` also passed Qwen3-VL-2B POSIX-VMM serving/abort/recovery, documentation checks and targeted FABRIC CI. Those results are retained as prior-head evidence, not relabeled as validation of this candidate.

## Performance — still draft

### Runtime-tested head `1a25c0a1`: completed, not accepted

On the same isolated B300 / pinned Qwen2.5-VL-3B revision and exact source above, compared admission unset versus 1000 ms. CUDA IPC, a sufficient **2 GiB pool in both arms**, default processor workers, preprocessing/radix caches off, CUDA graphs off, fixed 1024-square inputs and fixed histories; 32 conversations × 8 turns, repeat/append images, concurrency 1/8, three alternating pairs. All **6,144 measured + 1,536 multimodal warmup requests** completed with 16 actual output tokens. Timings, input hashes, prompt counts and zero cache hits were independently rechecked. Guarded CPU-spill counters stayed zero and publication gauges drained; legacy lacks these counters and is not reported as measured zero.

Paired-median change (guarded relative to legacy; positive latency is worse):

| Workload | Throughput | Hot p50 TTFT | Hot p95 TTFT | p95 E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Repeat, c1 | +1.02% | -1.64% | -1.46% | -0.99% |
| Repeat, c8 | +0.97% | **+13.52%** | +1.36% | +0.88% |
| Append, c1 | +1.10% | -0.95% | -0.54% | -3.61% |
| Append, c8 | -0.47% | **+8.22%** | -0.28% | -1.30% |

Repeat-c8 hot p50 regressed in **all three pairs: +12.59%, +13.52%, +15.83%**. Its third pair also lost 6.17% throughput with +13.87% hot p95 TTFT and +14.80% p95 E2E. Median throughput therefore does not establish acceptance or erase tail variation.

At c1, all 256 fixed inputs per scenario produced the same strings across all six runs. At c8, repeat/append had 15/9 variable inputs respectively; every observed cross-arm output set overlapped, with no stable arm-specific or disjoint output found in these three repeats. String equality nevertheless failed; this is not token/logit/embedding bitwise parity or proof that transport cannot affect correctness.

The original wrapper exited 0 and GPU memory returned to zero. The 2 GiB setting isolates normal-load admission overhead: it is **not a new recommended default**, a total preprocessing-memory cap, or a substitute for pressure/recovery tests. The 1 GiB preflight fit only five simultaneous maximum-size requests in this matrix. This result blocks draft promotion; the cause of the TTFT regression is not yet established.

### Earlier-head evidence

Same-commit admission-off/on replay; Qwen2.5-VL-3B, TP1, CUDA IPC, 64 MiB pool, preprocessing and radix caches off, CUDA graphs off, 448-square image, up to 8 output tokens.

The earlier `33b57e7` candidate's three-repeat c1/c8 matrix, with default and two processor workers, completed 6,144 measured requests with correct answers. Median throughput changes were -0.10%, +1.20%, -1.08%, +2.10%, respectively. However, default-worker c8 p95 E2E increased 33.1% in that shorter replay; this result remains recorded.

A longer, uninstrumented default-worker c8 replay used three alternating repetitions, 192 warmups and 1,024 measured requests per mode/repetition: all 6,144 measured requests passed.

| Metric | Admission off, median [range] | Admission on, median [range] |
|---|---:|---:|
| Requests/s | 80.883 [80.624–81.173] | 92.163 [88.933–95.857] |
| p95 E2E, ms | 104.205 [103.588–104.417] | 105.628 [104.213–107.834] |

This replay shows +13.95% median throughput and +1.37% median p95; it does not establish a universal speedup or explain away the earlier tail variability. The old public head's 9.53% default-worker / 3.73% two-worker throughput regressions are not substituted for candidate measurements.

Separate diagnostic timing found admission itself inexpensive (mean/p95 0.104/0.130 ms), while synchronous preprocessing delayed publication completion delivery on the event loop. Moving preprocessing to one off-loop worker reduced that delay but regressed end-to-end throughput in the diagnostic pair, so that experiment was **not** adopted. Instrumented timings are not pooled with the acceptance replay.

## Remaining gates

Keep draft. Runtime-tested head `1a25c0a1` CPU/IPC/VMM/H100 scoped tests and lint passed; this does not resolve performance acceptance. That source's c8 TTFT gate failed and remains unresolved. Broader workload/tail validation, full Kimi-K3/GLM, multi-node MNNVL/EPD and incident-shaped long soak are not established by these Qwen TP1 runs. No universal output/embedding bitwise-parity claim.

Native decoder memory accounting remains separate: a direct nvJPEG 13.0.1 hardware-decoder probe, without nvImageCodec, also bypassed a 16 MiB allocator-callback budget. An 8192-square JPEG increased observed device usage by 174.625 MiB with zero allocator callbacks (phase snapshots, not peak profiling). A hybrid-backend positive control did invoke and enforce the callback; changing backends would change decoded bytes. Publication admission cannot be advertised as a total preprocessing HBM cap or a complete OOM/hang fix.

## CI

Runtime-tested `1a25c0a1`: [CPU, 705 tests across ten files](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862006189), [5090 IPC, 14 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862032973), and [GB300 VMM, 21 tests including FABRIC/POSIX cross-GPU cases](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862058313) passed with exact source checkouts and no test skips. [Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42861386633) passed on PR merge `bb363157a2`. [H100 Qwen2.5-VL-7B serving](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862086005) passed all seven requested tests on the exact source: image-prefix reuse, mixed batch, single/multi-image, multi-turn, video and video+image. Its launch uses the existing default admission policy, so it is not a guarded-pressure test. Rust workspace runtime/build jobs were skipped on this follow-up; the isolated native checks above remain the runtime evidence. Exact-source documentation build and broken-link checks passed. The IPC producer-lifetime warning is retained; no leak-free soak or two-node validation claim.

Previous `67d60e2` passed [CPU, 54 tests across three files](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42732007085), [5090 IPC, 14 tests including worker cancellation and ready-write failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42732022452), [H100 Qwen input-format serving, 4 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42732038121), and [lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42731911330). All three test logs confirm checkout `67d60e286f91de5004dd43b1fa95733b800d1f9b`. The IPC producer-lifetime teardown warning remains recorded. Native/Rust change-detection workflows finished but skipped their runtime/build jobs on this follow-up; they are not counted as new Rust validation. This scoped result does not remove the remaining draft gates.

Pre-merge `33b57e7` scoped CI passed: [CPU, 668 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690843241), [IPC, 12 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690864250), [GB300 VMM, 21 tests including FABRIC round-trip/recycling](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690885872), and [MRoPE session serving](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690908210). This resolves that head's scoped FABRIC coverage gap, not full-model/multi-node validation.

Previous head `4af21ca` passed [CPU, 668 tests across nine files](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42696598137), [IPC, 12 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42696620111), [GB300 VMM, 21 tests including FABRIC round-trip/recycling](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42696642714), [MRoPE session serving](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42696679329), [Rust workspace](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42696527285), and [lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42696374742). Test checkout SHAs were verified. Automatic draft/opt-in gate failures do not mean the affected runtime tests executed; this is not a claim of full CI or merge readiness. No full unrelated CI matrix was requested.

issue.title: [Feat] diffusion/minimax-h3: Add an online FP8 video VAE decoder

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in, lossy FP8 **video VAE decoder profile for `quality="high"`** on MiniMax-H3. The 144 attention/FFN linears in the 36 decoder blocks use per-channel E4M3 weights, per-token activation scales, shared FP8 GEMM dispatch, and fused normalization/activation/quantization producers. Encoder weights, norms, the attention core and output projection keep their original precision.

### Quality and memory contract

- `--component-quantizations.video_vae fp8` enables the capability; it does not quantize at startup. Only a `high` request temporarily installs FP8 linears for decode.
- `exact` and `lossless` retain their existing paths and original weights. The original module objects/storage are restored in `finally`, including partial conversion failures, decode errors and cancellation. No FP8 weight cache survives a request.
- No additional FP8 GPU allocations for loading or non-high requests. High holds the originals plus temporary FP8 weights: approximately 2.25 GiB of payload plus workspace, measured at +2.45 GiB runtime peak in the workload below. The CUDA allocator can retain freed blocks in its reserved pool afterward.
- The FP8 high profile changes only decode, not the denoise trajectory. It does not mount Cache-DiT; explicitly combining the two is rejected. Without the FP8 flag, the existing H200 high profile is unchanged.
- CUDA SM100+, resident video VAE, default FP16 decode autocast, eager execution. Compile/BCG, component precision overrides and ignored-layer overrides are rejected. Weight updates between requests remain supported and the next high request quantizes the new weights; updates during an active FP8 decode are rejected before writes.

The original shared FP8 kernels, producer fusion, and resident decode-dtype-store fixes are retained. The earlier permanent-at-load implementation and its SM120 benchmark results do **not** describe the current request-scoped contract.

## Validation

Dedicated 1x B300, 275,040 MiB VRAM, driver 595.91.07; torch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0, sglang-kernel 0.4.10, FlashInfer 0.7.3. Host: Xeon 6787P, container CPU quota 36.55 cores, RAM limit 468.5 GiB. Public `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3` FL2VA checkpoint revision `42ed227ee7df40d41602854ae760620d6eb651fe`. Measurements below use `14effcea202a` after merging main `790cc4636f8d` and adopting its unified CUDA architecture API.

- CPU integration: **349 passed, 204 subtests passed** (admission, VAE loader/store, weight update, server args and fast-path policy).
- GPU: **25 passed** (FP8 decoder/producers) plus **27 passed** (H3 FP16 norm/output regressions), using all four registered test-file entry points.
- Full 36-block GPU switching test checks original parameter identity/storage and exact live allocation recovery, including exception/cancellation/partial-install recovery.
- Real offline E2E: three neutral prompts/seeds, 5 steps, 768p 16:9, 4-second target, 107 output frames, batch 1. Baseline 12 requests; FP8-enabled deployment 18 requests with `exact -> lossless -> high -> lossless -> high -> exact` for each prompt.
- Every non-high raw video is bit-identical to its corresponding no-flag baseline, including after high. Audio is tested separately with rtol=0 / atol=1e-7: the no-FP8 cold/warm baseline itself has max absolute roundoff 2.79e-8. No claim of universal audio bitwise determinism.
- High vs FP16 lossless: **worst-frame PSNR >=48.0659 dB, SSIM >=0.995178** across the three prompts. This is measured fidelity, not a universal quality guarantee or lossless claim.

### Performance and memory

5-step runs, default video-VAE attention, `performance_mode=speed`, compile off. Exclude the first invocation of each quality in each deployment; n=5 measured calls per row. Times are medians. Decode includes quantization/restoration; full request includes output delivery and MP4 writing.

| Deployment / request | Decode | Full request | Runtime peak allocated |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| No FP8 flag / exact | 2.668 s | 16.504 s | 118.57 GiB |
| FP8 flag / exact | 2.669 s | 16.497 s | 118.57 GiB |
| No FP8 flag / lossless | 1.754 s | 15.490 s | 120.98 GiB |
| FP8 flag / lossless | 1.754 s | 15.614 s | 120.98 GiB |
| FP8 flag / high | 1.548 s | 15.335 s | 123.42 GiB |

High is approximately **11.8% faster in decode, 1.8% faster end to end** than FP16 lossless within the FP8-enabled deployment (1.0% E2E against the no-flag deployment). Non-high decode timings are unchanged within noise; the small full-request variation is not evidence of a universal performance guarantee. Per-request allocated peaks use `after_forward.peak_allocated_mb`, not the cumulative `runtime_peak` snapshot.

Startup peak allocated/reserved is exactly the same with and without the flag: **127631.04 / 127772 MiB**. The first exact and lossless peaks also match exactly. High's live allocations are released before the next request; reserved pool grows from 127120 to 128694 MiB after high (+1.54 GiB). No claim that post-high reserved memory stays unchanged.

Reproducible harness: `test/manual/perf/bench_h3_fp8_quality.py` (run once normally, then with `--fp8` and the same output directory; `--steps 50 --vae-attention torch_cudnn_sdpa` selects the longer comparison). Comparisons use raw frames before lossy file encoding. The cookbook and CLI reference describe eligibility, switching, memory cost and limitations. No ground-truth updates.

### 50-step check

Same hardware/checkpoint/shape, one prompt, explicit `video_vae=torch_cudnn_sdpa`, four baseline requests and six FP8-deployment requests. All passed. The no-FP8 baseline's repeated exact audio differed by max 2.384e-7, so this run explicitly used `--audio-atol 3e-7`, rtol=0; the harness default remains 1e-7. All non-high raw video stays bit-exact, including the final exact request after two high decodes. High audio matches the lossless reference exactly in this sample.

| FP8-enabled deployment | Warm decode | Full request |
|---|---:|---:|
| lossless | 1.762 s | 101.362 s |
| high | 1.301 s | 100.844 s |

After excluding the first invocation of each quality, there is **one** warm sample per row: decode -26.2%, full request -0.5%. This is a longer-workload confirmation, not statistically conclusive E2E acceleration. High worst-frame PSNR/SSIM: **52.7266 dB / 0.998237**. Startup/default memory is unchanged; high has the same temporary-memory tradeoff as the 5-step run. The no-flag warm lossless reference was 1.761 s decode / 101.386 s total.

## Limits

Current request-scoped E2E evidence is on B300/FL2VA T2VA. Other SM100+ devices, conditioning tasks, longer videos and production concurrency are not claimed as covered by these results. FP8 remains explicit opt-in and high-only. The registered kernel tests run on the B200 lane; CI status below is independent of these development-machine measurements.

issue.title: [Feat] multimodal: Add bounded GPU feature publication admission
issue.body:
## Summary

Add opt-in, bounded admission for CUDA IPC/VMM feature publication. Related to #43402; this does **not** fix its CUDA-driver hang or cap upstream decoder/preprocessing allocations.

- Reserve the whole publication batch atomically, accounting for alignment, fragmentation and IPC control slots. Wait without holding partial slices or occupying the copy worker.
- `--mm-admission-timeout-ms 0` rejects on pressure; positive values wait up to the deadline. Oversized batches return 413, temporary pressure 429. HTTP/OpenAI/SSE and Python/Rust gRPC preserve these errors.
- Publish asynchronously on an ordered copy stream. Retain original and contiguous/native tensor owners until device copy completion, including cancellation and failed dispatch. Do not allocate a contiguous copy before a failed reservation.
- Preserve ACK/generation semantics and VMM packing; expose pool, pending, lease-lifetime and reclamation diagnostics. Include VLM, server-argument and K3 usage documentation.

Unset preserves existing behavior. No default backend/transport change, additional HBM pool, or silent CPU fallback on the guarded path. PD/EPD is outside this opt-in implementation.

## Development validation

### Stream-context cleanup follow-up: `cede5e31`

Protect the whole CUDA stream context around guarded publication. Before publication starts, context construction/entry errors return reservations; after publication succeeds, context-exit errors cancel every returned proxy through the existing ready/ACK lifecycle. Pool-owned publication failures retain their own rollback, avoiding double release. Failed cancellation retains the poisoned lease instead of reusing memory while a copy may still be in flight. No new synchronization, scheduling fast path, backend policy or CPU fallback is introduced.

Exact-source validation on an isolated single B300 (driver 580.126.20) passed **740 CPU tests + 616 subtests**, **23 GPU tests + 4 subtests**, and **12 real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B Engine input/identity tests** across CPU, legacy IPC and guarded IPC with two processor workers. **15 cross-GPU VMM tests were skipped** because at least three GPUs are required; the single-device guarded VMM case ran. Final exits were zero and device usage returned to zero. The IPC producer-lifetime warning remains recorded.

The same tests on the previous production source reproduce both pre-publication context failures and both post-publication cleanup assertions; the existing copy-failure double-release guard passes both versions. Context errors are injected at the external API boundary around real allocator/copy/ACK/recycler operations, not a reproduction of a corrupted CUDA driver. Logs, native exit codes and source hashes are preserved and verified. This correctness fix does **not** resolve the performance gate, establish cross-mode bitwise output parity, or justify removing draft. New-head targeted CI is requested separately.

Test-only follow-up `416c35d1e84766897adc060ba72848e2f4e202ac` fixes abort-test expectations that read proxy fields after cleanup had cleared them. The tests now snapshot the original proxies before execution, assert the exact cancellation sequence, and assert both fields are cleared. Clean published parent `e2441d3` reproduced all three intended assertion failures; the fixed head passed both full related CPU files (**72 tests + 47 subtests**, zero failures/errors/skips) on isolated development hardware. Production source is unchanged; this does not resolve the performance gate. [Targeted CPU CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42897376154) passed on an explicitly verified checkout of `416c35d1`: 60 manager tests and 12 abort-cleanup cases, with no failures or skips. [Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42897173617) passed on synthetic merge `f507aa1e10`, which includes this head. No new GPU or Rust runtime result is claimed for this test-only follow-up.

Documentation-only follow-up `e2441d34764184647eb83490a2ba2fefeec4c143` clarifies cancellation, in-flight publication and safe pool reclamation. Runtime source is unchanged from `1a25c0a1`; all runtime and performance results below retain that tested-head attribution. Changed-file pre-commit, Mintlify build validation and internal link/anchor/redirect checks passed locally (Node 24.22.1, Mint 4.2.559). New-head Mintlify deployment and link checks passed. [Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42889365134) passed on synthetic merge `292faeb2c6` (including `e2441d3`), with pre-commit, offline references, all 67 cookbook checks and Mintlify links passing. No GPU rerun was requested for this paragraph; these docs checks do not resolve the performance gate.

### Updated validation: `1a25c0a104c5e2e799cf9b06412fae8d39903cf5`

Resolved the argument-field-order conflict with a normal merge of main `2d93fbfe`; existing argument positions and the admission option are preserved. The following checks ran against the exact merged source on an isolated single B300 (driver 580.126.20, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, torchvision 0.29.2, Transformers 5.19.0):

- 15 CPU test files: **739 tests + 614 subtests passed**.
- Complete CUDA IPC/VMM transport test files: **20 tests + 4 subtests passed**; **15 multi-GPU VMM cases skipped** because only one GPU was available. The real single-device guarded VMM case ran; this is not cross-device/FABRIC coverage.
- Real Qwen2.5-VL HF processor comparison: **60 calls, 48 exact comparisons passed**, covering worker modes, cache on/off, image order/duplicates and RGB/RGBA input.
- Four real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B Engine input/identity tests in each of CPU transport, legacy CUDA IPC and guarded CUDA IPC: **12 cases passed**, with two processor workers.
- Native `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p sglang-grpc --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and **19 `sglang-grpc` library tests passed**.

All exit markers were zero; logs and source/model provenance were preserved and SHA256-verified. An IPC producer-lifetime warning remains in the raw output, so these checks are not a leak-free soak claim.

**Keeping this PR draft:** the exact-head normal-serving replay completed, but concurrency-8 TTFT failed the performance gate (details below). These functional results do not establish performance acceptance, full K3/EPD/MNNVL validation, a physical decoder/preprocessing HBM cap, or a fix for the production CUDA driver hang. One intermediate validation harness expected only one negative-control failure and stopped; that failed attempt is retained, and the final harness verifies both intended assertions without weakening the tests.

IPC producer-lifetime teardown warnings remain recorded. This is not a long soak or a new performance/full-K3/EPD/MNNVL result; legacy pool-miss D2H fallback remains part of publication and is not claimed to be off-loop.

Previous merge head `4af21ca298697bcccb9f830b018e99d7e2513332` normally merges pinned main `6d143e51b2a4`. The only manual conflict resolution preserves main's positional field order and appends the new admission argument afterward.

Fifteen cross-GPU VMM tests require at least three GPUs and were skipped on the single-card development box, not counted as passes. All jobs exited 0 and GPU memory returned to zero. - Nine CPU-hidden interface/configuration/cleanup/metrics files: 668 tests + 577 subtests passed.
- Five transport/configuration files: 132 passed; the explicit FABRIC test failed with `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED(800)`. This is missing coverage, not a green run. CUDA IPC and local POSIX VMM cases passed. An IPC producer-lifetime warning remains recorded at teardown.

All **6,144 measured + 1,536 multimodal warmup requests** completed with 16 actual output tokens. Timings, input hashes, prompt counts and zero cache hits were independently rechecked. Guarded CPU-spill counters stayed zero and publication gauges drained; legacy lacks these counters and is not reported as measured zero.

Paired-median change (guarded relative to legacy; positive latency is worse):

| Workload | Throughput | Hot p50 TTFT | Hot p95 TTFT | p95 E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Repeat, c1 | +1.02% | -1.64% | -1.46% | -0.99% |
| Repeat, c8 | +0.97% | **+13.52%** | +1.36% | +0.88% |
| Append, c1 | +1.10% | -0.95% | -0.54% | -3.61% |
| Append, c8 | -0.47% | **+8.22%** | -0.28% | -1.30% |

|---|---:|---:|
| Requests/s | 80.883 [80.624–81.173] | 92.163 [88.933–95.857] |
| p95 E2E, ms | 104.205 [103.588–104.417] | 105.628 [104.213–107.834] |

Add opt-in, bounded admission for CUDA IPC/VMM feature publication. Related to #43402; this does **not** fix its CUDA-driver hang or cap upstream decoder/preprocessing allocations.

- `--mm-admission-timeout-ms 0` rejects on pressure; positive values wait up to the deadline. Oversized batches return 413, temporary pressure 429. HTTP/OpenAI/SSE and Python/Rust gRPC preserve these errors.
- Publish asynchronously on an ordered copy stream. Retain original and contiguous/native tensor owners until device copy completion, including cancellation and failed dispatch. Do not allocate a contiguous copy before a failed reservation.
- Preserve ACK/generation semantics and VMM packing; expose pool, pending, lease-lifetime and reclamation diagnostics. Include VLM, server-argument and K3 usage documentation.

Unset preserves existing behavior. No default backend/transport change, additional HBM pool, or silent CPU fallback on the guarded path. PD/EPD is outside this opt-in implementation.

Before publication starts, context construction/entry errors return reservations; after publication succeeds, context-exit errors cancel every returned proxy through the existing ready/ACK lifecycle. Pool-owned publication failures retain their own rollback, avoiding double release. Failed cancellation retains the poisoned lease instead of reusing memory while a copy may still be in flight.
