issue.body: ## Motivation A Cosmos 3 request with `n > 1` (number of output per request) only returns one output, with HTTP 200. `Cosmos3Config` does not turn on the sequential multi-output path, and the first stage of `Cosmos3Pipeline` does not split the request, so the pipeline runs once. ## Modifications - `Cosmos3Config` turns on `supports_sequential_multi_output_inference`. Its subclasses (CosmosDreams, Cosmos3Multiview, Cosmos3SimAuto) use other pipelines and keep it off. These subclasses and disaggregated serving are unchanged and they will still return one output for `n > 1` - `Cosmos3ImagePreprocessStage.iter_sequential_requests` splits the request with `expand_request_outputs`, so output `i` uses seed `s + i` - Policy and inverse-dynamics requests reject `n > 1`, since `generate_action` returns only the first prediction ## Accuracy Tests The CI cases `cosmos3_nano_t2i` and `cosmos3_nano_t2v` (`test/server/gpu_cases.py`) with `n` added: same server flags and request bodies, running Cosmos 3 Edge on one DGX Spark. Each output is compared with an `n=1` request at seed `s + i`. | Request | main | This PR | |-|-|-| | `cosmos3_nano_t2i`, n=2 | 1 image | 2 images, pixel-identical to n=1 seeds 0 and 1 | | `cosmos3_nano_t2i`, n=4 | 1 image | 4 images, pixel-identical to n=1 seeds 0 to 3 | | `cosmos3_nano_t2v`, n=2 | 1 video | 2 videos, frame-identical to n=1 seeds 0 and 1 | | I2V, n=2 | 1 video | 2 videos, frame-identical to n=1 seeds 1111 and 1112 | | Every n=1 request | | bit-identical to original code | Since there is no I2V CI case, so the I2V row uses the cookbook image-to-video request with the checkpoint's `assets/example_i2v_input.jpg`, at the `cosmos3_nano_t2v` size, frames and steps. One cosmos3_nano_t2i request with n=4 and seed 0 returns these four images, from seeds 0 to 3: ## Speed Tests and Profiling `n=1` requests skip the new path: `cosmos3_nano_t2i` takes 6.34 s on main and 6.38 s with this PR. The `n` outputs run one after another, so time grows with `n`: | Request | n=1 | n=2 | n=4 | |-|-|-|-| | `cosmos3_nano_t2i` | 6.38 s | 12.79 s | 25.55 s | | `cosmos3_nano_t2v` | 2.88 s | 5.75 s | 11.50 s | | I2V | 4.23 s | 8.42 s | 16.92 s | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. issue.title: [Perf] cosmos: optimize bf16 fa

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual repeatedly runs non-causal, rectangular GQA with short queries and a growing KV history. The two dominant shapes at the cache limit are:

| Phase | Q shape | K/V shape |
|---|---|---|
| Denoise | `[1, 448, 32, 128]` | `[1, 14999, 8, 128]` |
| Clean-frame KV commit | `[1, 224, 32, 128]` | `[1, 14775, 8, 128]` |

The current PyTorch SDPA baseline is less efficient for these BF16 shapes on RTX PRO 6000. This PR exposes FlashInfer FA2 as a diffusion attention backend and uses it for the validated model/architecture combination.

## Modifications

- Add `flashinfer_fa2`, backed by `flashinfer.single_prefill_with_kv_cache(backend="fa2")`, with BSHD inputs, GQA, strided Q/K/V, FP16/BF16, and independent batch elements.
- Prefer it for Cosmos3 Dreams generation attention on SM12x. Preserve explicit backend overrides and fallback when FlashInfer is unavailable. The generic backend resolver has no architecture whitelist.
- Add backend-selection and GPU correctness tests, plus backend documentation.

## Accuracy Tests

- All 7 GPU correctness cases passed against FP32 PyTorch math SDPA (`atol=2e-3`, `rtol=2e-2`), covering growing/saturated KV, strided GQA, batch isolation, FP16/BF16, and causal masking.
- Checked 21 real model inputs against FP64 attention, sampling 16 query rows per input with all heads and the full KV sequence. Worst relative L2 error: **0.2313%** for FlashInfer FA2, versus **0.1722%** for PyTorch SDPA and Dao-AILab FA2.
- A full 901-frame Bimanual generation completed through the integrated backend. End-to-end task-quality equivalence has not been established; outputs are not guaranteed to be bitwise identical across backends.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, 96 GB, SM120; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.18. BF16, batch 1, 32 Q heads / 8 KV heads, head dimension 128, non-causal.

### Attention operators

Complete attention latency in microseconds, including SplitKV merge and any required conversions. CUDA events measure GPU execution with cold-cache inputs.

| Implementation | Q448 / KV14999 (µs) | Speedup vs SDPA | Q224 / KV14775 (µs) | Speedup vs SDPA |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **PyTorch SDPA — baseline** | **400.80** | **1.000×** | **259.87** | **1.000×** |
| Dao-AILab FA2 | 391.78 | 1.023× | 253.92 | 1.023× |
| **FlashInfer single FA2 — this PR** | **335.49** | **1.195×** | **184.77** | **1.406×** |
| FlashInfer ragged FA2 | 369.66 | 1.084× | 194.56 | 1.336× |
| cuDNN attention | 496.61 | 0.807× | 483.33 | 0.538× |
| PyTorch FlexAttention | 798.72 | 0.502× | 784.38 | 0.331× |
| Dao-AILab FA4 | 499.71 | 0.802× | 487.42 | 0.533× |
| SGLang SM120 FA4 | 558.08 | 0.718× | 280.54 | 0.926× |

FlashInfer FA2 achieves **1.195× / 1.406×** speedup over SDPA for the two shapes. Nsight Systems confirms that SDPA, Dao-AILab FA2, and FlashInfer FA2 each launch a main attention kernel and a merge kernel; both are included in the measurements.

### End-to-end generation

Paired measurements of this integrated backend on the same physical RTX PRO 6000: official Bimanual samples, request canvas **832×480**, cropped output **640×352**, **901 frames at 30 FPS**, four denoising steps, guidance 1.0, seed 2026, KV window 64 with 8 sink frames. CPU offload, Torch compile, and BCG were disabled; KV management, VAE overlap, and FFmpeg/libx264 output encoding were identical between runs.

Each backend ran in a separate process with **one full warmup using different image/action/prompt inputs, followed by one timed request**. Both used the same target inputs. SDPA was selected through the GEN attention override; FlashInfer FA2 used the model's automatic backend selection. Timing includes preprocessing, inference, VAE decoding, video encoding, and file completion, excluding model loading.

| Backend | End-to-end time | Speedup vs SDPA |
|---|---:|---:|
| PyTorch SDPA | 39.677 s | 1.000× |
| FlashInfer FA2 | **38.136 s** | **1.040×** |

This saves **1.541 s**, reducing request latency by **3.88%**. These are single-request measurements with unlocked GPU clocks. Mean SM clocks were 2354 / 2355 MHz, with no recorded thermal throttling in either timed request.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

issue.title: [Fix] CI: Avoid coverage fail-fast cycles on diffusion reruns

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
A failed `diffusion-coverage-check` can prevent an individual producer-job rerun from reaching its tests. Coverage consumes those producer reports, so treating its previous failure as a root cause creates a fail-fast cycle. This occurred in [#49078’s 5090 rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42379972109/job/128458495252).

Exclude the coverage summary from sibling root-failure detection. Lint and actual test failures still stop sibling jobs; the final coverage check remains required and continues to fail for missing reports or failed cases. This change does not alter memory/performance thresholds or fix the original memory failure.

issue.body:
## Motivation

Running community ComfyUI workflows on an SGLD model in integrated mode exposed three problems in the ComfyUI plugin:

1. **LoRAs from the previous prompt on a rebuilt worker.** ComfyUI reuses a cached MODEL across prompts, and its SGLD executor remembers the LoRAs it served last. When the worker was rebuilt before a sampler run, those LoRAs were loaded again and only then unmerged. A run started from the previous prompt's adapters.
2. **Silently dropped LoRAs.** The stock `LoraLoader` already fails on an SGLD model, but third-party LoRA or weight-patch nodes that call `model.add_patches()` directly stored patches the SGLD worker never applies. Their LoRA was dropped silently.
3. **Manual conversion.** Community workflows load an SGLD-servable DiT with the stock `UNETLoader` and add stock LoRA and speed-patch nodes. Moving such a workflow to SGLD meant swapping nodes by hand.

The PR has one commit per problem, which can be reviewed in order. All changes stay in `apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion/` and its tests.

## Modifications

**1. `[Fix] comfyui: Load this run's LoRAs into a rebuilt worker`**
- `SGLDiffusionGenerator.ensure_executor(executor, lora_input=...)` loads the given LoRAs into a rebuilt worker. It clears the executor's record first, because a fresh worker has none. Mid-run rebuilds still resend the adapters last set.
- The sampler wrapper passes the run's `sgld_lora_input`.

**2. `[Fix] comfyui: Reject ComfyUI weight patches on SGLD models`**
- `SGLDModelPatcher.add_patches()` raises on any non-empty patch set and points at `SGLDLoraLoader`. `SGLDLoraLoader` records worker-side adapters directly, so it is unaffected.
- The sampling-time patch-rejection error now says what to do with speed-only nodes: remove them and set the equivalent in `SGLDOptions`.

**3. `[Feat] comfyui: Add an offline workflow converter for SGLD models`**

`python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.apps.ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion.convert workflow.json` writes `<name>_sgld.json` and a markdown report.

Changed:
- `UNETLoader` / `UnetLoaderGGUF` with an H3 / Qwen-Image / Z-Image / FLUX.1 file → `SGLDUNETLoader`, also inside subgraphs. `weight_dtype` is reset to `default`, the only value the worker serves, and the reset is reported.
- `LoraLoaderModelOnly` / `LoraLoader` → `SGLDLoraLoader`, only when their MODEL traces back to an SGLD loader. Tracing goes through reroutes, subgraphs and KJNodes Set/Get pairs.
  - A LoRA on another model is left alone; an untraceable one is reported.
  - `LoraLoader`'s CLIP consumers are wired to its CLIP input. Its text-encoder half is not applied, and the report says so.

Reported, not changed:
- MODEL→MODEL nodes on the SGLD model, typically speed patches. Detection is generic, with no speed-node mapping table. Sampler-only nodes are not reported.
- LoRA stack nodes (rgthree, AusBoss, LoraManager): replace them by hand with chained `SGLDLoraLoader` nodes.

Also:
- Handles UI JSON (0.4 and v1 with subgraphs) and API JSON.
- Adds no node or link ids, and a converted workflow converts to itself.
- Nothing depends on what is installed on the converting machine.
- The runtime LoRA / patch errors name the converter.
- README: a "Converting a workflow" section.

## Accuracy Tests

All ComfyUI unit suites (`test_comfyui_*.py`) on H200: **266 passed**, 3 xfailed.

- `test_comfyui_lora_node.py`:
  - Through `sampler_sample_wrapper` with the real `ensure_executor`, a rebuilt worker loads only this run's LoRAs. This test fails if the wrapper drops `lora_input`.
  - `add_patches` rejects weight patches. This test fails without the override.
- `test_comfyui_convert.py` (12 tests) uses fixtures shaped like real UI and API exports and covers:
  - loader swap, in and out of subgraphs;
  - LoRA rewrite and CLIP rewiring;
  - LoRAs on non-SGLD models left alone;
  - an untraceable LoRA reported;
  - Set/Get tracing;
  - speed and stack nodes reported;
  - the `weight_dtype` reset;
  - idempotency;
  - the bundled SGLD workflows needing no changes;
  - the CLI.
- Converter only, on 60 real community workflows (Civitai, RunningHub, LiblibAI, official templates):
  - all 60 convert;
  - 67 loaders swapped, 31 LoRA nodes rewritten;
  - 44 workflows get reminders for 69 speed/DiT patch nodes and 21 LoRA stack nodes;
  - 1 LoRA is reported as untraceable.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation (ComfyUI README).

issue.title: [Perf] [ROCM] diffusion: Ring attention on aiter, and reuse the ring's K/V buffers

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

run of MiniMax-H3 on MI355X (sglang v0.5.23) takes 118.2 s on 2 GPUs, 36% more GPU-seconds than on 1 GPU (B200: 6%). Two GPUs exchange over a single XGMI link (~57 GB/s), so Ulysses' all-to-all is large next to the layer: even with the head-group pipeline (#47567), the first group's input exchange and the last group's output exchange stay exposed, about 5 ms of a ~46 ms layer on main.

Ring attention at degree 2 sends K/V once, overlaps the send with the local chunk's attention, and has no output exchange. `--ring-degree` refused aiter, though, and aiter is the fast exact backend on ROCm.

## Modifications

- aiter returns the softmax LSE the ring merge needs: `forward(..., return_softmax_lse=True)` (dense, `[B, H, S]`) and `forward_ring_kv_chunk` (packed, `[H, Tq]`), and declares `supports_ring_rotation()`. The LSE is fp32 natural log (checked against an fp32 reference).
- Server args and MiniMax-H3 (pipeline admission and the DiT's ring gate) accept aiter for ring.
- `_ring_attention_varlen` takes its stacked K/V pair from the reusable staging buffers instead of allocating a pair per call. A fresh pair stays held for the P2P stream until the GPU reaches it, and with the host hundreds of layers ahead that is one ~1 GB pair per queued layer: H3 at ring 2 ran out of device memory within 4 denoise steps (`HSA_STATUS_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`, also reproduced in a standalone loop). This part is backend-independent and leaves the values unchanged.
- Docs: the ring-capable backend list.

## Accuracy Tests

- Unit (ROCm with aiter): two KV chunks merged with the ring merge equal one call over all keys, on the packed and the dense path. Admission tests for aiter under ring. The new cases fail on main.
- End to end (H3 T2VA, 1344x768, 124 frames, 49 steps): ring 2 output is deterministic (same MP4 md5 across runs). Per-frame RGB PSNR against the 1-GPU output: ring 2 19.5 dB, Ulysses 2 18.7 dB; ring 2 against Ulysses 2 20.9 dB. Two different prompts are 6.6 dB apart, so ring sits in the same cross-topology floating-point reordering class as Ulysses.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X had no free capacity, so this ran on 8x MI350X (same gfx950 and 8-way XGMI mesh; 2-GPU all-reduce 56.7 GB/s vs 55.0 on MI355X). `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.23-rocm720-mi35x` with main `ba5906471` or this branch on `PYTHONPATH`, the recipe's flags (aiter, `--performance-mode speed`, eager), H3 T2VA 1344x768, 124 frames, 49 steps, 1 warmup + 3 prompts, client wall clock with 0.1 s polling, median. Four 2-GPU servers ran at once on the pairs 0-1/2-3/4-5/6-7, so each arm is compared on the same pair.

| 2 GPUs | GPUs 0-1 | GPUs 4-5 |
|---|---|---|
| v0.5.23, Ulysses 2 | 140.65 (pair 2-3) | |
| main, Ulysses 2 | 117.70 | 115.22 |
| this PR, ring 2 | **104.51 (-11.2%)** | **105.52 (-8.4%)** |

1 GPU takes 204 s, so ring 2 is within 2.5% of half of it.

Ring only helps where Ulysses has one link: on 4 GPUs Ulysses 4 (59.47 s) stays faster than Ulysses 2 x ring 2 (66.97 s), and on 8 GPUs Ulysses 8 (31.22 s) stays faster than Ulysses 4 x ring 2 (32.43 s).

On main, more pipeline groups (4 groups of 7 heads at Ulysses 2) save 1 ms per layer in a microbenchmark but nothing end to end (0.25%), and peer copies on the copy engine run at 28 GB/s on this machine, half of RCCL, so neither replaces ring here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit config (isort / ruff / black pass).
- [x] Add unit tests (merged into the existing test files for the touched area).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (above).

issue.title: [Perf] multimodal_cache: reuse precomputed combined_hash in MultiModalStaticCache.get

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

`MultiModalStaticCache.get` accepts a precomputed combined key, but overwrites it by calling `combine_hashes` again. The normal scheduler and encoder prefix-cache paths already build that key immediately before lookup.

After #47120, this key is an ordered tuple of complete typed media identities, not a compact `hash(tuple(...))`. This PR removes redundant key construction without changing the identities, their order, or cache hit/miss semantics.

## Changes

- Honor `combined_hash` when supplied; keep computing it for callers that omit it.
- Reuse the existing key in the normal scheduler and encoder prefix-cache lookup.
- Test actual cached embedding results, reordered-media misses, and the number of key constructions in both callers.

## Validation

- Head `957381e64298becf507a99cdb889b098efca71f4`, compared with pinned main `7c8ada7ec6890b045245adac4787b410be5ac909`.
- Isolated Linux CPU environment, Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 with no visible CUDA device: all three related files passed **75 tests plus 26 subtests** (chunked MM embeddings, encoder server, feature identity). The actual Rust radix-tree extension was built from this checkout for the identity tests.
- Both new regression tests fail on main for the intended redundant key-construction assertions; the same tests pass on the candidate. Cached embeddings and ordered identity semantics are asserted, not just mock call counts.
- Warm lookup microbenchmark, nine samples of 100,000 iterations per case, same CPU environment: median time for caller key construction + lookup was 206 -> 157 ns (1 item), 231 -> 185 ns (4), and 650 -> 528 ns (64). This is a small component optimization, **not an end-to-end throughput or TTFT claim**.
- Targeted pre-commit and diff checks passed. Logs, exit codes, scripts and source provenance are retained. The first collection attempt lacked a source-built Rust extension; it is preserved separately from the successful rerun.
- New GPU development validation is blocked by platform storage provisioning. No full-model, EPD/MNNVL, or GPU performance acceptance is claimed; scoped CI is requested separately.

## Credit

Original implementation by @deep1blue (Parth Vadera); the original authored commit is preserved. The follow-up adapts its regression coverage to the complete identity representation now on main and adds encoder-path coverage.

issue.title: [Perf] multimodal_cache: reuse precomputed combined_hash in MultiModalStaticCache.get

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

`MultiModalStaticCache.get` accepts a precomputed combined key, but overwrites it by calling `combine_hashes` again. The normal scheduler and encoder prefix-cache paths already build that key immediately before lookup.

After #47120, this key is an ordered tuple of complete typed media identities, not a compact `hash(tuple(...))`. This PR removes redundant key construction without changing the identities, their order, or cache hit/miss semantics.

## Changes

- Honor `combined_hash` when supplied; keep computing it for callers that omit it.
- Reuse the existing key in the normal scheduler and encoder prefix-cache lookup.
- Test actual cached embedding results, reordered-media misses, and the number of key constructions in both callers.

## Validation

- Head `957381e64298becf507a99cdb889b098efca71f4`, compared with pinned main `7c8ada7ec6890b045245adac4787b410be5ac909`.
- Isolated Linux CPU environment, Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 with no visible CUDA device: all three related files passed **75 tests plus 26 subtests** (chunked MM embeddings, encoder server, feature identity). The actual Rust radix-tree extension was built from this checkout for the identity tests.
- Both new regression tests fail on main for the intended redundant key-construction assertions; the same tests pass on the candidate. Cached embeddings and ordered identity semantics are asserted, not just mock call counts.
- Warm lookup microbenchmark, nine samples of 100,000 iterations per case, same CPU environment: median time for caller key construction + lookup was 206 -> 157 ns (1 item), 231 -> 185 ns (4), and 650 -> 528 ns (64). This is a small component optimization, **not an end-to-end throughput or TTFT claim**.
- Targeted pre-commit and diff checks passed. Logs, exit codes, scripts and source provenance are retained. The first collection attempt lacked a source-built Rust extension; it is preserved separately from the successful rerun.
- New GPU development validation is blocked by platform storage provisioning. No full-model, EPD/MNNVL, or GPU performance acceptance is claimed; scoped CI is requested separately.

## Credit

Original implementation by @deep1blue (Parth Vadera); the original authored commit is preserved. The follow-up adapts its regression coverage to the complete identity representation now on main and adds encoder-path coverage.

issue.title: [Fix] diffusion: Count reclaimable page cache as available inside a cgroup cap

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

Inside a memory-capped cgroup, `physical_host_memory_available_bytes()` took the cgroup's `memory.current` as used. That number includes the page cache charged to the cgroup, which the kernel reclaims under the cap. Outside a cgroup the same function uses psutil's `available` (MemAvailable), which counts that cache as available. So the two paths disagreed.

Seen on an RTX 5090 desktop with 60 GB RAM, MiniMax-H3 T2VA 480p, run in `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=56G` right after another engine ran in the same scope:

| | host memory log | DiT layers pinned | denoise |
|---|---|---|---|
| no cgroup | 41.5 GiB available | 32 / 50 | 4.55 s/it |
| 56G scope | 17.6 GiB available (cap 56.0, in use 38.4) | 12 / 50 | 5.12 s/it |

A container started with `--memory` hits the same thing, since the checkpoint it reads at load is charged to it as cache. The Ascend server-test conftest evicts stale model cache before each case to work around the same reading.

## Modifications

- Inside a cap, usage now excludes the file LRUs: `active_file + inactive_file` on v2, and `total_active_file + total_inactive_file` on v1 (v1 `usage_in_bytes` covers the subtree; the unprefixed keys do not). This matches what MemAvailable counts. shmem/tmpfs stays counted as used. It is in v2's `file` and v1's `cache`, which the old shared-pool path subtracted, but only swap can reclaim it.
- `shared_pool_available_bytes()` became identical to the physical reading, so it is removed and its one caller uses `physical_host_memory_available_bytes()`.
- The startup line now shows how much of the cgroup usage is reclaimable cache.

Why not subtract only `inactive_file` (the kubelet working set):
- Which list a page is on depends on how it was accessed and on the LRU implementation. MGLRU reports the young generations as active, and the classic LRU lets the active list grow to about sqrt(10 * GB) times the inactive one. Cold leftover cache can therefore sit on the active list, and the bug would stay.
- `page_cache_cannot_hold()` would count a hot, already-cached mapping as used. A courier rebuilt after LoRA would then switch to O_DIRECT reads for a mapping the cache already holds.

Counting a mapping's own cached pages as available does not let a placement evict the mapping it streams from:
- The planner leaves a layer on its mapping only when the copies do not fit. Each byte pinned out of the mapping is then a byte the mapping no longer needs cached.
- The readings that size anonymous or pinned memory (pin budget, layer plan, loader, AdaLN host tier) all run at load or configure time, before any mapping streams.

## Tests

`test_host_memory_budget.py` has a new `TestCgroupPageCache` that fakes `memory.max`, `memory.current` and `memory.stat`:
- cache left in a capped cgroup counts as available (the bug)
- a mapping the cache already holds on the active list is room for itself (rules out the inactive-only rewrite)
- shmem charged to the cgroup is not available (rules out a rewrite to `file`)
- v1 subtracts subtree totals

All four fail on main and pass here. I also checked each guard by mutation: inactive-only, `file`/`cache`, and v1 local keys are each caught. The whole file passes locally (36 tests, CPU). The layerwise offload, weight snapshot and component residency tests stub these functions; they need the full kernel stack, so CI runs them.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not rerun. The 5090 host went offline before the scoped A/B. The expected result is the uncapped numbers above (about 41 GiB available, about 32 pins).

## Follow-up

Once this lands, the Ascend conftest's per-case cache eviction (`test/server/ascend/conftest.py`) should no longer be needed for the budget reading. That file is left as is here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation (none describes this reading).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (no output change; A/B pending, see above).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

issue.body:
## Motivation

#47120 has merged. This PR now targets main with only the three-file Kimi follow-up (+125/-13): the shared Kimi helper, its regression tests, and one valid-fingerprint test fixture.

Kimi's raw-image source/config/grid identity is still needed: a strong tensor hash does not identify preprocessing configuration or permit an early source-cache lookup. This PR preserves that fast path and uses the shared typed identity for prepared inputs instead of a second model-specific implementation.

The previous fallback snapshots a feature or embedding to CPU and combines it with the processor fingerprint and grid. Equal tensors can therefore alias across input formats or different deferred preprocessing metadata. The new regressions reproduce false embedding-cache hits on the parent implementation.

## Changes

- Use the common full identity for prepared/no-source inputs, including feature versus embedding role, input format, shape/dtype, encoder metadata and processor fingerprint.
- Keep raw-image source/config/grid hashing unchanged. Do not remove K3 preprocessing-cache protections or weaken digests.
- Preserve payload/grid validation and ignore stale scalar hints when recomputing a prepared item's identity.
- Add real embedding-cache hit/miss tests, including K3 deferred normalization/backend metadata, and common-identity parity coverage.

No new flags, decoder/resize changes, or radix-cache policy changes. Safe common-prefix reuse is a separate follow-up; the parent's whole-request media namespace remains intact here.

## Validation

Current head `afd322ee6827` normally merges the already-merged #47120 (`7828f5670110`) into the child. The three remaining diff files are byte-identical to the preceding child head; no new production behavior was added by the merge.

Exact-head validation on an isolated NVIDIA B300, Python 3.12.16 / PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 / Transformers 5.19.0:

- CPU-hidden Kimi identity, K2.5, common feature identity and artifact processor files: **106 passed + 37 passing subtests**.
- GPU Kimi/common identity, BLAKE3 and CUDA IPC files: **53 passed + 167 passing subtests**.
- The unchanged regression assertions against the exact merged-main Kimi helper still produce **4 expected assertion failures** (3 methods), covering format/deferred-metadata aliasing and the unwanted CPU snapshot. This is a helper-level negative control, not a full main-server run.
- The actual K3 prepared-input parser/finalizer -> pooled IPC -> spawned consumer probe passed: full identity, feature values, offsets and zero outstanding leases. Final validation exit 0; ending GPU memory/utilization 0 MiB/0%.
- Changed-file pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

The first negative-control harness attempt stopped because the test retry wrapper converted assertions into generic errors; the corrected harness preserves the original assertions and canonical snapshot-spy target. Both attempts are retained. An IPC producer-lifetime warning was observed; the results above are not a leak-free-soak claim. No new full-weight Kimi serving, cross-node/EPD or performance result is claimed. Exact-head targeted CI is requested separately.


### Earlier implementation validation

Dedicated NVIDIA H200, Python 3.12.16, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. Candidate: `e496fcf587f3c70b2b212f3cbd3b41b859f88282`; parent production: `d33ea169ef09506b161df4c5ea54897435b19fb0`.

- Parent reproduced wrong cache hits for input format and deferred normalization/backend changes, plus the unwanted CPU snapshot path. These were assertion failures, not setup failures.
- Candidate CPU-hidden: **56 passed, 37 passing subtests** across Kimi identity, common feature identity, media artifact and K3 encoder-mode suites.
- Candidate CUDA-visible Kimi identity suite: **24 passed, 12 passing subtests**.
- Actual Python/Rust radix caches at page sizes 1 and 16: **16 hit/miss checks passed**. The parent reproduced a wrong KV hit when only the prepared-input format changed; same-input reuse is retained by the candidate.
- K3's real prepared-input parser/finalizer -> pooled CUDA IPC -> spawned consumer passed: full identity, feature values, grid/offsets and zero outstanding pool leases. This probe does not load model weights.
- CPU/GPU full identity agreement at 1, 16 and 64 MiB. Raw-source fast path still makes no feature-sized D2H copy.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks passed.

Prepared-input hash microbenchmark, 5 warmups and 30 synchronized samples per size:

| GPU feature | Parent median | Candidate median | D2H payload, parent -> candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 MiB | 1.100 ms | 0.184 ms | 1 MiB -> 32 B |
| 16 MiB | 22.304 ms | 0.179 ms | 16 MiB -> 32 B |
| 64 MiB | 112.802 ms | 0.244 ms | 64 MiB -> 32 B |

This measures only the prepared-input identity step, not raw-image serving, full-weight Kimi throughput, or cross-node EPD. CPU metadata and the feature remain identical; only the computed cache identity changes as intended. GPU hashing still uses temporary scratch space and synchronization.

issue.title: Modify data_hash to use full SHA-256 digest

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: The PR is ready to merge after the CI is green.

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body: ## Motivation identified a security vulnerability in the data_hash function. Currently, the function truncates the SHA-256 hash to the first 64 bits (8 bytes). Furthermore, when used as a cache key, it relies on Python's built-in hash(), which further reduces the security entropy to approximately 2^61. This truncation drasticially reduces collision resistance, enabling the construction of adversarial images that share the same hash. This vulnerability could be exploited to bypass image moderation filters or perform cache poisoning. By removing the [:8] truncation and returning the full hash value, we significantly improve security and prevent these collisions. Additionally, by introducing a string component to the hash input, we increase the randomness of the cache key, preventing attackers from pre-computing cache values. Note: This PR is a preliminary solution. A collision issue caused by **pad_value** still exists, but is not addressed in this PR as fixing the limited pad value space would require extensive code modifications. ## Modifications Updated data_hash to return the complete SHA-256 hash string instead of a truncated version. I investigated the usage of this function and confirmed it is primarily used for cache key generation in schedule_batch.py, so it will not affect other components: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/842807843671e1f469fe272a3f69a5582925004b/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L254 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/842807843671e1f469fe272a3f69a5582925004b/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L288 Full Hash Return: Updated data_hash to return the complete SHA-256 hash string instead of the truncated version. Randomized Cache Keys: Changed the return statement from return hash(tuple(mm_hashes)) to return hash(("random_seed", tuple(mm_hashes))). This change ensures that cache keys differ across processes, mitigating predictability. ## Accuracy Tests I tested the changes using Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct. Inference: Normal inference functionality is preserved. Collision Resolution: The system can now correctly distinguish between the collision images that previously generated identical hashes Test Images (Hash Collision Proof of Concept): ## Benchmarking and Profiling The impact on performance is negligible, as the change only involves storing and comparing slightly longer string keys (full hash vs. truncated) during cache lookups. **Distributed Context:** The inclusion of the string makes cache keys inconsistent across different processes. While this creates a risk of non-reusability in multi-node sharing, SGLang's current image caching mechanism is single-node/local. Therefore, this does not constitute a functional or security regression. **Reference:** This issue is similar to the vulnerability found in vLLM (GHSA-rm76-4mrf-v9r8), and the adopted solution follows a similar approach.

comment.body:
Thanks @kexinoh for reporting the digest truncation/composite-key collision problem and documenting a reproduction. #47120 has now merged with full 256-bit typed identities, full ordered composite keys (rather than using Python's reduced `hash(...)` as equality), and a complete-media namespace for KV reuse. The shared feature path uses CPU/GPU BLAKE3-256; this is an alternative implementation, not an application of this patch.

Closing this as superseded by the merged fix. Your analysis of the lossy-key boundary was valuable; the merged fix also addresses the partial-padding/KV identity limitation noted in this PR.

issue.title: [Fix] VLM: Rebuild padded input ids after caller mm_hashes

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

A request that sends caller `mm_hashes` with an image crashes the scheduler on a cold cache (`index_copy_(): index out of bounds`), and the server stops. On a warm cache it does not crash, but it ignores the caller hash, so an external KV-aware router that sends hashes never gets a prefix match. The cause: the processor (for example Qwen3-VL) builds `padded_input_ids` from its own hash. `TokenizerManager` then applies the caller hash with `set_hash`, which changes each item's pad values but not `padded_input_ids`, and the scheduler reuses the stale ids. This PR rebuilds the ids after `set_hash`, with the same builder that the processors use. Setting the ids to `None` (#40225) also stops the crash, but it moves padding back into the scheduler, which #26097 and #36411 removed on purpose.

## Modifications

- After `TokenizerManager` applies caller hashes, it rebuilds `padded_input_ids` with `MultimodalProcessorOutput.build_padded_input_ids`, if the processor built them. Other processors see no change.
- A new unit test checks that the caller-derived pads reach the processor-built ids.

## Accuracy Tests

Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct on one GPU, tokens-in `/generate` with `image_data`, main at 5ed306bd69 vs this PR merged with it. "Caller pads" are the pad values that `set_hash` derives from the caller hash.

| Same image, caller `mm_hashes` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Cold cache | Scheduler crash: `index_copy_(): index out of bounds` | 200, KV event carries the caller pads |
| Cached before without hashes | 200, cached_tokens 208 (caller hash ignored) | 200, cached_tokens 0, KV event carries the caller pads |
| Same request again | Not run (server down) | 200, cached_tokens 208 |

Requests without `mm_hashes` are unchanged: same caption, 213 prompt tokens and the processor's own pads in the KV event. Unit: all 13 tests in `test_mm_hashes.py` pass with hash precompute off and on, and the new test fails on main.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The fix adds one list rebuild per request that has caller hashes and processor-built ids.

issue.title: [Fix] multimodal: Gate caller mm_hashes behind --trust-caller-mm-hashes
issue.body:
Thanks for the thorough report and the reproducer, @yyymk — the cross-tenant disclosure angle makes this worth fixing properly.

Fixes #44641.

## Root cause

The native `/generate` endpoint accepts a caller-declared `mm_hashes` field, and `TokenizerManager` applied it unconditionally to each `MultimodalDataItem` via `item.set_hash(int(hex_hash, 16))`. Since `MultimodalDataItem.hash` determines `pad_value` (`schedule_batch.py`), and the image region of the token sequence is that pad value repeated, the declared hash *is* the prefix-cache identity of the image segment. A request sending image B but declaring image A's hash produced A's token sequence for the image region and hit A's cached KV — silent wrong-image reuse, with the radix cache shared across tenants. The embedding path never had this problem: `EmbeddingReqInput` has no `mm_hashes` field at all (the #34411 precedent).

## Fix

Caller-declared `mm_hashes` are now honored only when the server is launched with the new opt-in flag `--trust-caller-mm-hashes`:

- Default (flag unset): caller `mm_hashes` are ignored (one warning per tokenizer worker), and the content-based hash is recomputed downstream via `set_pad_value()` → `hash_feature()`, as before.
- Flag set: today's behavior is preserved exactly (same length check, same per-item parse fallback) for the external-KV-router use case the field was built for.

Design invariants:

1. A caller-declared hash must never become a cache identity by default — it is untrusted input from the network, and the radix cache is shared across tenants.
2. The flag is the *only* gate: there is no per-request allowlist, no partial application. With the flag off, `MultimodalDataItem.hash` stays `None` until the content hash is computed, so no code path can observe the declared value.
3. Malformed input never blocks a request: length mismatch ignores the whole list, a bad hex entry falls back per item (unchanged from before).
4. `mm_content_hashes` (SHA-256 content identities, already gated by `--trust-mm-content-hashes`) are untouched.

## Reproducer (unit-level; no GPU on this machine)

I don't have a GPU here, so I verified at the logic level: the real `MultimodalDataItem` class and the real `_apply_caller_mm_hashes` method, extracted verbatim from the repo files, driven with mock multimodal items. Scenario: request sends image B (content hash `0xAAAA...0002`) but declares image A's hash (`0xDEADBEEF...0001`).

```
=== BEFORE (pre-fix code): caller hash applied unconditionally ===
old code, image B declares A's hash: item.hash=0xdeadbeef00000001 pad_value=1000001
pad_value derived from declared hash => prefix-cache identity = image A (pad matches A's own: True)

=== AFTER (fixed code): default --trust-caller-mm-hashes unset ===
WARNING Ignoring caller-provided mm_hashes: --trust-caller-mm-hashes is not set, ...
new code flag OFF, image B declares A's hash: item.hash=0xaaaa0000bbbb0002 pad_value=1003110978
caller hash ignored: item.hash is content hash of B (True), pad matches B's own: True

=== AFTER (fixed code): --trust-caller-mm-hashes set (KV-router use case) ===
new code flag ON, image B declares A's hash: item.hash=0xdeadbeef00000001 pad_value=1000001
caller hash honored: True, pad matches old behavior: True

=== edge cases (fixed code) ===
length mismatch (2 hashes, 1 item): ignored -> hash=None
malformed entry: ignored -> hash=None
no mm_hashes field value: untouched -> hash=None
obj without mm_hashes attr (EmbeddingReqInput-like): untouched -> hash=None
```

These are verbatim outputs of the script; the before/after comparison shows the declared hash no longer controls the pad value (prefix-cache identity) by default, and the flag restores the old behavior bit-for-bit.

## Tests

New regression tests in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_mm_hashes.py` (`TestCallerMmHashesGating`), exercising `TokenizerManager._apply_caller_mm_hashes` directly: ignored-by-default, honored-with-flag, length-mismatch, malformed entry, no-mm_hashes noop.

```
$ python -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_mm_hashes.py -q
13 passed in 14.19s   # 8 pre-existing + 5 new
```

Also ran `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`: 277 passed; 3 failures (`TestGrpcServerArgs::test_start_server_call_site_matches_native_signature`, `TestParserChoices::test_a_plugin_registered_parser_is_accepted`, `TestLazyReexports::test_the_names_that_lost_their_eager_import_are_still_attributes`) are pre-existing on the unmodified base (verified via `git stash`) and unrelated to this change.

Verified the CLI wiring: `--trust-caller-mm-hashes` registers, defaults to `False`, sets `True` when passed.

## Notes

issue.title: [CI] rerun-test: Retry diffusion reruns like the multimodal-gen CI

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

`/rerun-test` on a diffusion test can fail on noise that the multimodal-gen CI job would have retried past.

The CI jobs run pytest through `sglang.multimodal_gen.test.runner.pytest_runner.run_pytest`. It retries failed items up to 6 times when the failure is retryable: a `[performance]` check, a timeout, an OOM. It stops starting new retries once `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_RETRY_DEADLINE` is reached. The `rerun-test-multimodal-gen` job runs bare `python3 -m pytest $cmd -x` instead, with no retry. That breaks the workflow's own goal ("so a rerun validates what CI actually ran"). CUDA reruns already retry once, through `CustomTestCase` with `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI`.

The timing checks in this suite are noisy. On main's scheduled runs of `multimodal-gen-test-2-gpu` since 10-12, at least one attempt failed a timing check in 37 of 45 runs, spread across 22 cases. The retry absorbed every one: none of the 6 job-level failures in that window came from a timing check.

Example: #47962 changed only the `ltx_2_two_stage_t2v` VRAM baseline. Two `/rerun-test` runs of `test_server_2_gpu.py` failed on unrelated LTX-2.3 timing checks:
- `ltx_2.3_one_stage_ti2v` TextEncodingStage: 789 ms against a 718 ms limit ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41556835219)).
- `ltx_2.3_two_stage_t2v_2gpus` E2E: 9389 ms against an 8158 ms limit ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41572697032)).

A third rerun, narrowed to just `ltx_2_two_stage_t2v`, passed.

## Modifications

In `rerun-test-multimodal-gen`'s "Run test" step:
- Run each command through `run_pytest` (with a JUnit file, so the deadline check can estimate how long the failed items take) instead of `python3 -m pytest $cmd -x`.
- Set `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_RETRY_DEADLINE` to 50 minutes from the step's start, as `pr-test-multimodal-gen.yml` does. The step timeout is 60 minutes. A whole-file rerun of `test_server_2_gpu.py` takes about 60 minutes on its own, so it gets no retries, as today. Narrower reruns get them.
- Drop `-x`, matching CI. With retries, `-x` would also be wrong: the retry pass runs only the last-failed items, so items after the first failure would never run.

Consistency-check failures (missing or mismatched ground truth) and other non-retryable failures still fail on the first attempt, as in CI.

## Testing

I ran the new command locally on dummy tests. In the test harness only, the import pointed at a copy of `pytest_runner.py`, since importing the `sglang` package needs torch.
- A `[performance]` failure that passes on its second run: exit 0 after one retry, and the other tests in the file still ran once.
- A plain `AssertionError`: exit 1, no retry.
- An expired deadline: exit 1, "Retry budget exhausted".
- The old `pytest -x` on the same file: exit 1, and the tests after the failure never ran.

A real check needs a `/rerun-test` of a diffusion test once this is on main, since the workflow runs from the default branch.

## Checklist

- [x] pre-commit passes (`check yaml`, `check-workflow-job-names`, `check-opt-in-ci-tiers`).

comment.body:
My concern is that a lot of the variability comes from differences between runners, rather than noise between attempts. Diffusion reruns can land on different runners, and we have seen substantial performance differences even within the same GPU class.

Since these automatic retries stay within the same job, they will keep using the same runner. If that runner is consistently slower than the one used to establish the baseline, all retries may still fail, leaving us manually triggering `/rerun-test` repeatedly until the job lands on a faster runner. A green result would then depend on placement rather than the code change.

I understand this PR aligns `/rerun-test` with the retry behavior already used by regular CI. But could we also address runner comparability? Otherwise, I worry that many diffusion performance checks will still require multiple manual reruns, with the automatic retries adding runtime without resolving the underlying issue.

Current conflict-resolution head `16b61eade952` normally merges pinned main `133f712a498e`. It preserves main's move of multimodal wire types into `managers/req_types.py` and relocates the complete strong-identity implementation there, without duplicate classes or an eager scheduler/identity import. - CPU-hidden identity/padding/cache and native Rust contracts: **114 tests + 81 subtests**, with one CUDA-only test skipped.
- GPU hash/IPC/request/abort contracts: **97 tests + 187 subtests**, no skips.
- GPU-visible identity tests plus the previously skipped cache case: **18 tests + 26 subtests**, no skips; 17 cases repeat CPU-covered tests in the GPU-visible environment.

All final phase exits were 0; changed-file pre-commit and scoped relocation checks passed. issue.body:
## Motivation

#47120 has merged. This PR now targets main with only the three-file Kimi follow-up (+125/-13): the shared Kimi helper, its regression tests, and one valid-fingerprint test fixture.

Kimi's raw-image source/config/grid identity is still needed: a strong tensor hash does not identify preprocessing configuration or permit an early source-cache lookup. This PR preserves that fast path and uses the shared typed identity for prepared inputs instead of a second model-specific implementation.

The previous fallback snapshots a feature or embedding to CPU and combines it with the processor fingerprint and grid. Equal tensors can therefore alias across input formats or different deferred preprocessing metadata. The new regressions reproduce false embedding-cache hits on the parent implementation.

## Changes

- Use the common full identity for prepared/no-source inputs, including feature versus embedding role, input format, shape/dtype, encoder metadata and processor fingerprint.
- Keep raw-image source/config/grid hashing unchanged. Do not remove K3 preprocessing-cache protections or weaken digests.
- Preserve payload/grid validation and ignore stale scalar hints when recomputing a prepared item's identity.
- Add real embedding-cache hit/miss tests, including K3 deferred normalization/backend metadata, and common-identity parity coverage.

No new flags, decoder/resize changes, or radix-cache policy changes. Safe common-prefix reuse is a separate follow-up; the parent's whole-request media namespace remains intact here.

## Validation

Current head `afd322ee6827` normally merges the already-merged #47120 (`7828f5670110`) into the child. The three remaining diff files are byte-identical to the preceding child head; no new production behavior was added by the merge.

Exact-head validation on an isolated NVIDIA B300, Python 3.12.16 / PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 / Transformers 5.19.0:

- CPU-hidden Kimi identity, K2.5, common feature identity and artifact processor files: **106 passed + 37 passing subtests**.
- GPU Kimi/common identity, BLAKE3 and CUDA IPC files: **53 passed + 167 passing subtests**.
- The unchanged regression assertions against the exact merged-main Kimi helper still produce **4 expected assertion failures** (3 methods), covering format/deferred-metadata aliasing and the unwanted CPU snapshot. This is a helper-level negative control, not a full main-server run.
- The actual K3 prepared-input parser/finalizer -> pooled IPC -> spawned consumer probe passed: full identity, feature values, offsets and zero outstanding leases. Final validation exit 0; ending GPU memory/utilization 0 MiB/0%.
- Changed-file pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

The first negative-control harness attempt stopped because the test retry wrapper converted assertions into generic errors; the corrected harness preserves the original assertions and canonical snapshot-spy target. Both attempts are retained. An IPC producer-lifetime warning was observed; the results above are not a leak-free-soak claim. No new full-weight Kimi serving, cross-node/EPD or performance result is claimed. Exact-head targeted CI is requested separately.


### Earlier implementation validation

Dedicated NVIDIA H200, Python 3.12.16, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. Candidate: `e496fcf587f3c70b2b212f3cbd3b41b859f88282`; parent production: `d33ea169ef09506b161df4c5ea54897435b19fb0`.

- Parent reproduced wrong cache hits for input format and deferred normalization/backend changes, plus the unwanted CPU snapshot path. These were assertion failures, not setup failures.
- Candidate CPU-hidden: **56 passed, 37 passing subtests** across Kimi identity, common feature identity, media artifact and K3 encoder-mode suites.
- Candidate CUDA-visible Kimi identity suite: **24 passed, 12 passing subtests**.
- Actual Python/Rust radix caches at page sizes 1 and 16: **16 hit/miss checks passed**. The parent reproduced a wrong KV hit when only the prepared-input format changed; same-input reuse is retained by the candidate.
- K3's real prepared-input parser/finalizer -> pooled CUDA IPC -> spawned consumer passed: full identity, feature values, grid/offsets and zero outstanding pool leases. This probe does not load model weights.
- CPU/GPU full identity agreement at 1, 16 and 64 MiB. Raw-source fast path still makes no feature-sized D2H copy.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks passed.

Prepared-input hash microbenchmark, 5 warmups and 30 synchronized samples per size:

| GPU feature | Parent median | Candidate median | D2H payload, parent -> candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 MiB | 1.100 ms | 0.184 ms | 1 MiB -> 32 B |
| 16 MiB | 22.304 ms | 0.179 ms | 16 MiB -> 32 B |
| 64 MiB | 112.802 ms | 0.244 ms | 64 MiB -> 32 B |

This measures only the prepared-input identity step, not raw-image serving, full-weight Kimi throughput, or cross-node EPD. CPU metadata and the feature remain identical; only the computed cache identity changes as intended. GPU hashing still uses temporary scratch space and synchronization.

## Checklist

- [x] Reproduce on parent and validate candidate on isolated development hardware
- [x] Preserve semantic structure and raw-source fast path
- [x] Formatting/lint
- [ ] Upstream CI

issue.title: [Feat] multimodal: Add bounded GPU feature publication admission
issue.body:
## Summary

Add opt-in, bounded admission for CUDA IPC/VMM feature publication. Related to #43402; this does **not** fix its CUDA-driver hang or cap upstream decoder/preprocessing allocations.

- Reserve the whole publication batch atomically, accounting for alignment, fragmentation and IPC control slots. Wait without holding partial slices or occupying the copy worker.
- `--mm-admission-timeout-ms 0` rejects on pressure; positive values wait up to the deadline. Oversized batches return 413, temporary pressure 429. HTTP/OpenAI/SSE and Python/Rust gRPC preserve these errors.
- Publish asynchronously on an ordered copy stream. Retain original and contiguous/native tensor owners until device copy completion, including cancellation and failed dispatch. Do not allocate a contiguous copy before a failed reservation.
- Preserve ACK/generation semantics and VMM packing; expose pool, pending, lease-lifetime and reclamation diagnostics. Include VLM, server-argument and K3 usage documentation.

Unset preserves existing behavior. No default backend/transport change, additional HBM pool, or silent CPU fallback on the guarded path. PD/EPD is outside this opt-in implementation.

## Development validation

### Stream-context cleanup follow-up: `cede5e31`

Protect the whole CUDA stream context around guarded publication. Before publication starts, context construction/entry errors return reservations; after publication succeeds, context-exit errors cancel every returned proxy through the existing ready/ACK lifecycle. Pool-owned publication failures retain their own rollback, avoiding double release. Failed cancellation retains the poisoned lease instead of reusing memory while a copy may still be in flight. No new synchronization, scheduling fast path, backend policy or CPU fallback is introduced.

Exact-source validation on an isolated single B300 (driver 580.126.20) passed **740 CPU tests + 616 subtests**, **23 GPU tests + 4 subtests**, and **12 real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B Engine input/identity tests** across CPU, legacy IPC and guarded IPC with two processor workers. **15 cross-GPU VMM tests were skipped** because at least three GPUs are required; the single-device guarded VMM case ran. Final exits were zero and device usage returned to zero. The IPC producer-lifetime warning remains recorded.

The same tests on the previous production source reproduce both pre-publication context failures and both post-publication cleanup assertions; the existing copy-failure double-release guard passes both versions. Context errors are injected at the external API boundary around real allocator/copy/ACK/recycler operations, not a reproduction of a corrupted CUDA driver. Logs, native exit codes and source hashes are preserved and verified. This correctness fix does **not** resolve the performance gate, establish cross-mode bitwise output parity, or justify removing draft. New-head targeted CI is requested separately.

Test-only follow-up `416c35d1e84766897adc060ba72848e2f4e202ac` fixes abort-test expectations that read proxy fields after cleanup had cleared them. The tests now snapshot the original proxies before execution, assert the exact cancellation sequence, and assert both fields are cleared. Clean published parent `e2441d3` reproduced all three intended assertion failures; the fixed head passed both full related CPU files (**72 tests + 47 subtests**, zero failures/errors/skips) on isolated development hardware. Production source is unchanged; this does not resolve the performance gate. [Targeted CPU CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42897376154) passed on an explicitly verified checkout of `416c35d1`: 60 manager tests and 12 abort-cleanup cases, with no failures or skips. [Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42897173617) passed on synthetic merge `f507aa1e10`, which includes this head. No new GPU or Rust runtime result is claimed for this test-only follow-up.

Documentation-only follow-up `e2441d34764184647eb83490a2ba2fefeec4c143` clarifies cancellation, in-flight publication and safe pool reclamation. Runtime source is unchanged from `1a25c0a1`; all runtime and performance results below retain that tested-head attribution. Changed-file pre-commit, Mintlify build validation and internal link/anchor/redirect checks passed locally (Node 24.22.1, Mint 4.2.559). New-head Mintlify deployment and link checks passed. [Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42889365134) passed on synthetic merge `292faeb2c6` (including `e2441d3`), with pre-commit, offline references, all 67 cookbook checks and Mintlify links passing. No GPU rerun was requested for this paragraph; these docs checks do not resolve the performance gate.

### Updated validation: `1a25c0a104c5e2e799cf9b06412fae8d39903cf5`

Resolved the argument-field-order conflict with a normal merge of main `2d93fbfe`; existing argument positions and the admission option are preserved. The following checks ran against the exact merged source on an isolated single B300 (driver 580.126.20, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, torchvision 0.29.2, Transformers 5.19.0):

- 15 CPU test files: **739 tests + 614 subtests passed**.
- Complete CUDA IPC/VMM transport test files: **20 tests + 4 subtests passed**; **15 multi-GPU VMM cases skipped** because only one GPU was available. The real single-device guarded VMM case ran; this is not cross-device/FABRIC coverage.
- Real Qwen2.5-VL HF processor comparison: **60 calls, 48 exact comparisons passed**, covering worker modes, cache on/off, image order/duplicates and RGB/RGBA input.
- Four real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B Engine input/identity tests in each of CPU transport, legacy CUDA IPC and guarded CUDA IPC: **12 cases passed**, with two processor workers.
- Native `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p sglang-grpc --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and **19 `sglang-grpc` library tests passed**.

All exit markers were zero; logs and source/model provenance were preserved and SHA256-verified. An IPC producer-lifetime warning remains in the raw output, so these checks are not a leak-free soak claim.

**Keeping this PR draft:** the exact-head normal-serving replay completed, but concurrency-8 TTFT failed the performance gate (details below). These functional results do not establish performance acceptance, full K3/EPD/MNNVL validation, a physical decoder/preprocessing HBM cap, or a fix for the production CUDA driver hang. Feature-pool admission is the scope of this PR; the separate full-preprocessor budget work is not included. Targeted CI must be assessed on this exact head separately from older-head results.

### Previous head

Previous head `67d60e286f91de5004dd43b1fa95733b800d1f9b` preserves the `7a68600` ready-write regression and adds a processor-worker cancellation fix. The worker prepares request-owned tensors; legacy IPC leases are published only after the awaiting caller receives the result. Hashing and normal CPU-transport copies stay on the original worker. Default worker/backend policy is unchanged.

On isolated B300 (driver 595.91.07), this exact head passed 724 CPU-hidden tests + 600 subtests, 20 single-card transport tests + 4 subtests (15 unsupported cross-GPU cases skipped), 60 pinned-HF calls with 48 exact comparisons, and all four real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B input-format cases in each of CPU, legacy IPC and guarded IPC modes with two processor workers. All final exits were 0; GPU memory returned to zero. The old `7a68600` source reproduces the orphaned lease and worker-side publication assertions. One intermediate validation harness expected only one negative-control failure and stopped; that failed attempt is retained, and the final harness verifies both intended assertions without weakening the tests.

IPC producer-lifetime teardown warnings remain recorded. This is not a long soak or a new performance/full-K3/EPD/MNNVL result; legacy pool-miss D2H fallback remains part of publication and is not claimed to be off-loop.

Previous merge head `4af21ca298697bcccb9f830b018e99d7e2513332` normally merges pinned main `6d143e51b2a4`. The only manual conflict resolution preserves main's positional field order and appends the new admission argument afterward.

Exact-head isolated B300 validation passed 668 CPU-hidden tests + 580 subtests; 18 single-card IPC/VMM tests + 2 subtests; ordinary/streaming session equivalence and three abort/drain/flush/recovery waves with each of one and two tokenizer workers; Linux Rust Clippy and all 19 gRPC unit tests. Fifteen cross-GPU VMM tests require at least three GPUs and were skipped on the single-card development box, not counted as passes. All jobs exited 0 and GPU memory returned to zero. The IPC producer-lifetime teardown warning remains recorded.

The following broader development/performance evidence is from pre-merge production head `33b57e7c3bf48cc4595f07b93ca66812180e21bf`, on isolated NVIDIA B300 hardware; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0, driver 580.126.20. It is not relabeled as a new-head performance replay.

- Nine CPU-hidden interface/configuration/cleanup/metrics files: 668 tests + 577 subtests passed.
- Five transport/configuration files: 132 passed; the explicit FABRIC test failed with `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED(800)`. This is missing coverage, not a green run. CUDA IPC and local POSIX VMM cases passed. An IPC producer-lifetime warning remains recorded at teardown.
- Negative controls on the earlier async candidate reproduce blocking publication and allocation before failed reservation. They do **not** directly reproduce a use-after-free or the production hang.
- Linux, repository-pinned Rust 1.92: workspace Clippy, multimodal Python/parallel Clippy, radix tch/doc-only Clippy, and all 19 gRPC unit tests passed. Other changed-file pre-commit checks passed; the macOS full-workspace build cannot compile existing Linux-only server APIs.
- Real-weight Qwen2.5-VL-3B, revision `66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3`: IPC normal serving, 413/429 pressure, gauge drain and correct recovery passed. Ten real-client disconnect waves also drained pool/pending gauges to zero. This is not a long soak.
- One and two tokenizer workers: ordinary/streaming sessions match independently salted full-history replay in output IDs and image-token counts; three 16-request abort/drain/flush/recovery waves per worker count passed. Pool budget is total across workers: an undersized two-worker configuration correctly returned 413. Successful lifecycle runs keep 16 MiB per worker (16/32 MiB total).

Prior-head `db2fb5d0` also passed Qwen3-VL-2B POSIX-VMM serving/abort/recovery, documentation checks and targeted FABRIC CI. Those results are retained as prior-head evidence, not relabeled as validation of this candidate.

## Performance — still draft

### Runtime-tested head `1a25c0a1`: completed, not accepted

On the same isolated B300 / pinned Qwen2.5-VL-3B revision and exact source above, compared admission unset versus 1000 ms. CUDA IPC, a sufficient **2 GiB pool in both arms**, default processor workers, preprocessing/radix caches off, CUDA graphs off, fixed 1024-square inputs and fixed histories; 32 conversations × 8 turns, repeat/append images, concurrency 1/8, three alternating pairs. All **6,144 measured + 1,536 multimodal warmup requests** completed with 16 actual output tokens. Timings, input hashes, prompt counts and zero cache hits were independently rechecked. Guarded CPU-spill counters stayed zero and publication gauges drained; legacy lacks these counters and is not reported as measured zero.

Paired-median change (guarded relative to legacy; positive latency is worse):

| Workload | Throughput | Hot p50 TTFT | Hot p95 TTFT | p95 E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Repeat, c1 | +1.02% | -1.64% | -1.46% | -0.99% |
| Repeat, c8 | +0.97% | **+13.52%** | +1.36% | +0.88% |
| Append, c1 | +1.10% | -0.95% | -0.54% | -3.61% |
| Append, c8 | -0.47% | **+8.22%** | -0.28% | -1.30% |

Repeat-c8 hot p50 regressed in **all three pairs: +12.59%, +13.52%, +15.83%**. Its third pair also lost 6.17% throughput with +13.87% hot p95 TTFT and +14.80% p95 E2E. Median throughput therefore does not establish acceptance or erase tail variation.

At c1, all 256 fixed inputs per scenario produced the same strings across all six runs. At c8, repeat/append had 15/9 variable inputs respectively; every observed cross-arm output set overlapped, with no stable arm-specific or disjoint output found in these three repeats. String equality nevertheless failed; this is not token/logit/embedding bitwise parity or proof that transport cannot affect correctness.

The original wrapper exited 0 and GPU memory returned to zero. The 2 GiB setting isolates normal-load admission overhead: it is **not a new recommended default**, a total preprocessing-memory cap, or a substitute for pressure/recovery tests. The 1 GiB preflight fit only five simultaneous maximum-size requests in this matrix. This result blocks draft promotion; the cause of the TTFT regression is not yet established.

### Earlier-head evidence

Same-commit admission-off/on replay; Qwen2.5-VL-3B, TP1, CUDA IPC, 64 MiB pool, preprocessing and radix caches off, CUDA graphs off, 448-square image, up to 8 output tokens.

The earlier `33b57e7` candidate's three-repeat c1/c8 matrix, with default and two processor workers, completed 6,144 measured requests with correct answers. Median throughput changes were -0.10%, +1.20%, -1.08%, +2.10%, respectively. However, default-worker c8 p95 E2E increased 33.1% in that shorter replay; this result remains recorded.

A longer, uninstrumented default-worker c8 replay used three alternating repetitions, 192 warmups and 1,024 measured requests per mode/repetition: all 6,144 measured requests passed.

| Metric | Admission off, median [range] | Admission on, median [range] |
|---|---:|---:|
| Requests/s | 80.883 [80.624–81.173] | 92.163 [88.933–95.857] |
| p95 E2E, ms | 104.205 [103.588–104.417] | 105.628 [104.213–107.834] |

This replay shows +13.95% median throughput and +1.37% median p95; it does not establish a universal speedup or explain away the earlier tail variability. The old public head's 9.53% default-worker / 3.73% two-worker throughput regressions are not substituted for candidate measurements.

Separate diagnostic timing found admission itself inexpensive (mean/p95 0.104/0.130 ms), while synchronous preprocessing delayed publication completion delivery on the event loop. Moving preprocessing to one off-loop worker reduced that delay but regressed end-to-end throughput in the diagnostic pair, so that experiment was **not** adopted. Instrumented timings are not pooled with the acceptance replay.

## Remaining gates

Keep draft. Runtime-tested head `1a25c0a1` CPU/IPC/VMM/H100 scoped tests and lint passed; this does not resolve performance acceptance. That source's c8 TTFT gate failed and remains unresolved. Broader workload/tail validation, full Kimi-K3/GLM, multi-node MNNVL/EPD and incident-shaped long soak are not established by these Qwen TP1 runs. No universal output/embedding bitwise-parity claim.

Native decoder memory accounting remains separate: a direct nvJPEG 13.0.1 hardware-decoder probe, without nvImageCodec, also bypassed a 16 MiB allocator-callback budget. An 8192-square JPEG increased observed device usage by 174.625 MiB with zero allocator callbacks (phase snapshots, not peak profiling). A hybrid-backend positive control did invoke and enforce the callback; changing backends would change decoded bytes. Publication admission cannot be advertised as a total preprocessing HBM cap or a complete OOM/hang fix.

## CI

Runtime-tested `1a25c0a1`: [CPU, 705 tests across ten files](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862006189), [5090 IPC, 14 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862032973), and [GB300 VMM, 21 tests including FABRIC/POSIX cross-GPU cases](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862058313) passed with exact source checkouts and no test skips. [Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42861386633) passed on PR merge `bb363157a2`. [H100 Qwen2.5-VL-7B serving](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42862086005) passed all seven requested tests on the exact source: image-prefix reuse, mixed batch, single/multi-image, multi-turn, video and video+image. Its launch uses the existing default admission policy, so it is not a guarded-pressure test. Rust workspace runtime/build jobs were skipped on this follow-up; the isolated native checks above remain the runtime evidence. Exact-source documentation build and broken-link checks passed. The IPC producer-lifetime warning is retained; no leak-free soak or two-node validation claim.

Previous `67d60e2` passed [CPU, 54 tests across three files](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42732007085), [5090 IPC, 14 tests including worker cancellation and ready-write failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42732022452), [H100 Qwen input-format serving, 4 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42732038121), and [lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42731911330). All three test logs confirm checkout `67d60e286f91de5004dd43b1fa95733b800d1f9b`. The IPC producer-lifetime teardown warning remains recorded. Native/Rust change-detection workflows finished but skipped their runtime/build jobs on this follow-up; they are not counted as new Rust validation. This scoped result does not remove the remaining draft gates.

Pre-merge `33b57e7` scoped CI passed: [CPU, 668 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690843241), [IPC, 12 tests](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690864250), [GB300 VMM, 21 tests including FABRIC round-trip/recycling](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690885872), and [MRoPE session serving](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/42690908210). This resolves that head's scoped FABRIC coverage gap, not full-model/multi-node validation.

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Summary

Make multimodal CUDA VMM transport opt-in, just like CUDA IPC. An unset
`--mm-feature-transport` now resolves to CPU on every topology, including
GB200/GB300 with IMEX. Explicit GPU transports and the deprecated IPC env opt-in
remain supported.

This avoids automatically reserving a GPU feature pool and exposing deployments
to the pool-full GPU-to-CPU fallback reported in #43402. Thanks to @StarDuster
for the report and native-stack evidence. The lifecycle fixes from #43475 are
already on main; **this is a safe-default mitigation, not a fix for the unresolved
CUDA D2H hang**, and must not close #43402.

Update CLI help, the K3 command picker, K3/GLM cookbooks and common VLM guidance:
the transport pool budget is not a GPU preprocessing peak-memory limit. Main
already accounts for the pool in the KV budget. CPU transport does not force
CPU-only decoding/preprocessing and can cost transfer latency; GPU transport is
still available for deployments that explicitly choose and validate it.

## Validation

- Original main + new regression: GB200/GB300 with IMEX both fail the intended
  CPU-default assertion. These are mocked topology-selection tests, not a real
  MNNVL deployment.
- Dedicated B200, driver 580.126.09, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0:
  430 unit tests + 206 subtests passed with CUDA hidden; 6 real CUDA IPC
  cross-process/lifecycle tests passed.
- Real-weight Qwen3.5-2B: default CPU and explicit IPC both start, expose the
  expected resolved setting, and answer four alternating/repeated red/blue image
  requests correctly (8 requests total). Both servers shut down; GPU use returned
  to 0 MiB. IPC teardown printed a PyTorch shared-tensor warning; this smoke does
  not establish long-running IPC/VMM lifetime correctness.
- Pre-commit, cookbook config validation, Mintlify build and broken-links passed.
  The build reports six warnings on unchanged pages.

Not validated: full K3, multi-node MNNVL/EPD, performance, or the incident's
aarch64/580.126.20 hang. The existing 15-case VMM GPU suite requires at least three
GPUs and was skipped on this one-GPU allocation.

issue.title: [Fix] kernels: Hash tensors over 8 GiB in gpu_tensor_hash

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

`gpu_tensor_hash` computes each tile's offset as `pid * TILE` in int32. For a tensor over 8 GiB (2**31 words), the offset wraps negative and the kernel reads before the buffer: `CUDA error: an illegal memory access`.

`/weights_checker` with `action=checksum` hashes every weight with this kernel, so it crashes the engine on any model with a tensor over 8 GiB per rank. We hit it on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP 8, where each rank's engram table slice is 12.3 GB.

## Modifications

- Compute the offset in int64. Tensors under 8 GiB hash to the same values as before.
- Add a test that hashes a tensor just over 8 GiB (it fails without the fix), and one that pins the hash of a small tensor.

## Accuracy Tests

The change affects hashing only, not model outputs. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (8×B300, TP 8, EP 8), the `/weights_checker` checksum failed before the fix. With the fix, it succeeds in 6.9 s and the engine stays healthy.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hashing a 4 GiB tensor on a B300 takes 2.94 ms before and 2.99 ms after (about 1.7% slower). The kernel isn't on the forward path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
