issue.title: [Fix] multimodal: Preserve strong identities across VLM caches

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: Pull requests that update a dependency file

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

Multimodal cache equality must depend on actual model-facing content, not a short scalar or a caller-provided hint. The old GPU reduction admits structured collisions, composite keys lose information through `hash(tuple(...))`, and matching only part of a media placeholder can still reuse unrelated KV state.

This is a correctness-first fix across the shared VLM paths, not a model-specific opt-in or a universal speedup claim.

## Modifications

- Add shared CPU/GPU BLAKE3-256 with typed shape/dtype/container/metadata identities. GPU tensors transfer only their digests to the host.
- Preserve full identities through embedding caching, batch deduplication, sessions, EPD and native Rust sidecars. Rust output digests use full SHA-256 and bind the serving configuration at ingress.
- Namespace KV requests using ordered full media identities and `cache_salt`. Short or partial placeholder matches cannot substitute for complete identity equality.
- Stop allowing caller `mm_hashes` to override content identity, including precomputed embeddings. Keep the separate explicit `--trust-mm-content-hashes` boundary documented.
- Preserve Kimi source/config/grid protections; cover composite processors and finalized OCR metadata. Reuse full Qwen/Muse artifact fingerprints on cache hits instead of rehashing their feature tensors.
- Add common-contract, kernel, native/transport and real Qwen input regressions, plus documentation of compatibility and prefix-sharing tradeoffs.

The GPU BLAKE3 kernel is adapted from @xupinjie's #46028; author credit is preserved. Related narrower work: #44653, #46552, #46815 and #47066. This PR does not modify diffusion conditioning caches or include #37537.

## Accuracy Tests

Current conflict-resolution head `16b61eade952` normally merges pinned main `133f712a498e`. It preserves main's move of multimodal wire types into `managers/req_types.py` and relocates the complete strong-identity implementation there, without duplicate classes or an eager scheduler/identity import. Full BLAKE3 and typed-identity hashing remain unchanged from the preceding PR head.

Exact-head validation on an isolated B300 (driver 590.48.01, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0) passed:

- CPU-hidden identity/padding/cache and native Rust contracts: **114 tests + 81 subtests**, with one CUDA-only test skipped.
- GPU hash/IPC/request/abort contracts: **97 tests + 187 subtests**, no skips.
- GPU-visible identity tests plus the previously skipped cache case: **18 tests + 26 subtests**, no skips; 17 cases repeat CPU-covered tests in the GPU-visible environment.

All final phase exits were 0; changed-file pre-commit and scoped relocation checks passed. The first CPU-hidden attempt failed collection because an existing test helper indexes an empty `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`; rerunning the same source with an out-of-range GPU ordinal and an explicit zero-device assertion passed. IPC teardown emitted a producer-lifetime warning; ending GPU memory/utilization were 0 MiB/0%. This is conflict-integration validation, not a new full-model, performance, multi-node or leak-free-soak claim. Current-head targeted CI is requested separately.

Previous delivery head `48150838db03` normally merges the pinned main commit containing #47835, fixing the two unrelated diffusion fixtures from the old CI snapshot. It preserves @g0djan's #47066 diagnostic-checksum fix and leaves full BLAKE3/typed VLM identity unchanged. Isolated B200 validation on this exact head passed **244 tests + 241 subtests**, exit 0: hash/identity (28 + 197 subtests), request/abort/Rust interface contracts (103 + 44 subtests), and four diffusion fixture/cache files (113). Runtime imports and freshly built extensions used this checkout; driver 580.126.09, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. This is merge-integration validation, not a new full-model serving or performance result.

Remote H200 validation, implementation `15884434708` (the following commit changes documentation only):

- **976 passed**, 23 skipped, 149 passing subtests: common CPU/processor/cache/session/encoder tests, including actual Python and Rust radix trees.
- **51 passed**, 133 passing subtests: GPU hash/IPC/VMM/encoder tests. One FABRIC test fails because this container returns `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`; POSIX fallback passes. The test is unchanged and normally runs on GB300.
- **2 passed**: native Rust encoded-sidecar tests. Native Python/Rust suite: 49 passed plus four PIL resize parity subtest failures reproduced on the pristine base; no tolerances or assertions changed.
- Real Qwen2.5-VL-3B: CPU and CUDA IPC, videos with caches enabled/disabled, raw/processor/precomputed inputs, A-B-A and concurrent isolation. Final existing input fixture: **4 passed**.
- Final native Rust HTTP and two-GPU Mooncake EPD: **23 requests passed each**, including ordered multi-image requests and identical caller hints. Earlier ZMQ EPD and global embedding store runs also passed 23 each.
- Real InternVL3.5-1B: **22 requests passed**. This is representative E2E coverage, not a claim that every VLM checkpoint was tested.
- CPU/GPU BLAKE3 reference agreement includes 15 crafted legacy collision pairs, length padding, noncontiguous inputs, streams, and a manual 8 GiB + 17 byte boundary check.

Qwen revision: `66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3`; InternVL revision: `2f71cf52542334823e48a46ffba0e2bc9add3446`. Environment: H200, driver 595.71.05, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8, Python 3.12.16, blake3 1.0.11, Rust 1.92. Multi-GPU EPD was same-host; cross-node and non-NVIDIA E2E remain untested. Zero observed collisions is not proof that collisions are impossible.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Matched Qwen serving: CUDA IPC, 64 MiB preprocess cache, context 8192, memory fraction 0.45, CUDA graphs off, max running 8, seed 37, one greedy output token. After three warmups: 33 changing images and 20 same-image requests. Baseline was repeated twice. Median milliseconds:

| Workload | Baseline changing | Candidate changing | Baseline same image | Candidate same image |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 224 image | 40.62-40.70 | 41.47 | 21.83-21.85 | 22.18 |
| 1024 image | 68.26-68.82 | 72.67 | 29.55-29.81 | 29.63 |
| Shared 2048-token text + 224 image | 41.07-41.14 | 42.66 | 22.44-22.74 | 22.74 |

Generated token IDs matched in these benchmark cases. Full identity checking adds work on changing-media requests. Different media deliberately no longer share their common text KV prefix; same ordered media still shares it. Long shared-prefix workloads can incur a larger prefill penalty.

Interleaved 100-sample GPU microbench, including host synchronization: 12 MiB raw BLAKE3 **0.099 ms**, typed identity **0.128 ms**, versus old GPU64 **0.100 ms** and D2H+CPU BLAKE3 **3.068 ms**. At 153 MiB, raw BLAKE3 is **0.301 ms** versus old GPU64 **0.237 ms**. This avoids feature-sized D2H, but is not uniformly faster than the old weak GPU hash. Dense hashing needs small scratch buffers; noncontiguous inputs require a contiguous copy. No saturated-throughput claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Changed-file pre-commit checks, including Rust format/clippy
- [x] Regression tests and representative real-model validation
- [x] Documentation, caller trust boundaries and performance tradeoffs
- [ ] Upstream CI

issue.title: [Fix] kernels: Hash tensors over 8 GiB in gpu_tensor_hash

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

`gpu_tensor_hash` computes each tile's offset as `pid * TILE` in int32. For a tensor over 8 GiB (2**31 words), the offset wraps negative and the kernel reads before the buffer: `CUDA error: an illegal memory access`.

`/weights_checker` with `action=checksum` hashes every weight with this kernel, so it crashes the engine on any model with a tensor over 8 GiB per rank. We hit it on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP 8, where each rank's engram table slice is 12.3 GB.

## Modifications

- Compute the offset in int64. Tensors under 8 GiB hash to the same values as before.
- Add a test that hashes a tensor just over 8 GiB (it fails without the fix), and one that pins the hash of a small tensor.

## Accuracy Tests

The change affects hashing only, not model outputs. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (8×B300, TP 8, EP 8), the `/weights_checker` checksum failed before the fix. With the fix, it succeeds in 6.9 s and the engine stays healthy.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hashing a 4 GiB tensor on a B300 takes 2.94 ms before and 2.99 ms after (about 1.7% slower). The kernel isn't on the forward path.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

issue.title: [Fix] multimodal: Preserve strong identities across VLM caches

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: Pull requests that update a dependency file

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

Multimodal cache equality must depend on actual model-facing content, not a short scalar or a caller-provided hint. The old GPU reduction admits structured collisions, composite keys lose information through `hash(tuple(...))`, and matching only part of a media placeholder can still reuse unrelated KV state.

This is a correctness-first fix across the shared VLM paths, not a model-specific opt-in or a universal speedup claim.

## Modifications

- Add shared CPU/GPU BLAKE3-256 with typed shape/dtype/container/metadata identities. GPU tensors transfer only their digests to the host.
- Preserve full identities through embedding caching, batch deduplication, sessions, EPD and native Rust sidecars. Rust output digests use full SHA-256 and bind the serving configuration at ingress.
- Namespace KV requests using ordered full media identities and `cache_salt`. Short or partial placeholder matches cannot substitute for complete identity equality.
- Stop allowing caller `mm_hashes` to override content identity, including precomputed embeddings. Keep the separate explicit `--trust-mm-content-hashes` boundary documented.
- Preserve Kimi source/config/grid protections; cover composite processors and finalized OCR metadata. Reuse full Qwen/Muse artifact fingerprints on cache hits instead of rehashing their feature tensors.
- Add common-contract, kernel, native/transport and real Qwen input regressions, plus documentation of compatibility and prefix-sharing tradeoffs.

The GPU BLAKE3 kernel is adapted from @xupinjie's #46028; author credit is preserved. Related narrower work: #44653, #46552, #46815 and #47066. This PR does not modify diffusion conditioning caches or include #37537.

## Accuracy Tests

Current conflict-resolution head `16b61eade952` normally merges pinned main `133f712a498e`. It preserves main's move of multimodal wire types into `managers/req_types.py` and relocates the complete strong-identity implementation there, without duplicate classes or an eager scheduler/identity import. Full BLAKE3 and typed-identity hashing remain unchanged from the preceding PR head.

Exact-head validation on an isolated B300 (driver 590.48.01, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Transformers 5.19.0) passed:

- CPU-hidden identity/padding/cache and native Rust contracts: **114 tests + 81 subtests**, with one CUDA-only test skipped.
- GPU hash/IPC/request/abort contracts: **97 tests + 187 subtests**, no skips.
- GPU-visible identity tests plus the previously skipped cache case: **18 tests + 26 subtests**, no skips; 17 cases repeat CPU-covered tests in the GPU-visible environment.

All final phase exits were 0; changed-file pre-commit and scoped relocation checks passed. The first CPU-hidden attempt failed collection because an existing test helper indexes an empty `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`; rerunning the same source with an out-of-range GPU ordinal and an explicit zero-device assertion passed. IPC teardown emitted a producer-lifetime warning; ending GPU memory/utilization were 0 MiB/0%. This is conflict-integration validation, not a new full-model, performance, multi-node or leak-free-soak claim. Current-head targeted CI is requested separately.

Previous delivery head `48150838db03` normally merges the pinned main commit containing #47835, fixing the two unrelated diffusion fixtures from the old CI snapshot. It preserves @g0djan's #47066 diagnostic-checksum fix and leaves full BLAKE3/typed VLM identity unchanged. Isolated B200 validation on this exact head passed **244 tests + 241 subtests**, exit 0: hash/identity (28 + 197 subtests), request/abort/Rust interface contracts (103 + 44 subtests), and four diffusion fixture/cache files (113). Runtime imports and freshly built extensions used this checkout; driver 580.126.09, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130. This is merge-integration validation, not a new full-model serving or performance result.

Remote H200 validation, implementation `15884434708` (the following commit changes documentation only):

- **976 passed**, 23 skipped, 149 passing subtests: common CPU/processor/cache/session/encoder tests, including actual Python and Rust radix trees.
- **51 passed**, 133 passing subtests: GPU hash/IPC/VMM/encoder tests. One FABRIC test fails because this container returns `CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`; POSIX fallback passes. The test is unchanged and normally runs on GB300.
- **2 passed**: native Rust encoded-sidecar tests. Native Python/Rust suite: 49 passed plus four PIL resize parity subtest failures reproduced on the pristine base; no tolerances or assertions changed.
- Real Qwen2.5-VL-3B: CPU and CUDA IPC, videos with caches enabled/disabled, raw/processor/precomputed inputs, A-B-A and concurrent isolation. Final existing input fixture: **4 passed**.
- Final native Rust HTTP and two-GPU Mooncake EPD: **23 requests passed each**, including ordered multi-image requests and identical caller hints. Earlier ZMQ EPD and global embedding store runs also passed 23 each.
- Real InternVL3.5-1B: **22 requests passed**. This is representative E2E coverage, not a claim that every VLM checkpoint was tested.
- CPU/GPU BLAKE3 reference agreement includes 15 crafted legacy collision pairs, length padding, noncontiguous inputs, streams, and a manual 8 GiB + 17 byte boundary check.

Qwen revision: `66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3`; InternVL revision: `2f71cf52542334823e48a46ffba0e2bc9add3446`. Environment: H200, driver 595.71.05, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, Triton 3.8, Python 3.12.16, blake3 1.0.11, Rust 1.92. Multi-GPU EPD was same-host; cross-node and non-NVIDIA E2E remain untested. Zero observed collisions is not proof that collisions are impossible.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Matched Qwen serving: CUDA IPC, 64 MiB preprocess cache, context 8192, memory fraction 0.45, CUDA graphs off, max running 8, seed 37, one greedy output token. After three warmups: 33 changing images and 20 same-image requests. Baseline was repeated twice. Median milliseconds:

| Workload | Baseline changing | Candidate changing | Baseline same image | Candidate same image |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 224 image | 40.62-40.70 | 41.47 | 21.83-21.85 | 22.18 |
| 1024 image | 68.26-68.82 | 72.67 | 29.55-29.81 | 29.63 |
| Shared 2048-token text + 224 image | 41.07-41.14 | 42.66 | 22.44-22.74 | 22.74 |

Generated token IDs matched in these benchmark cases. Full identity checking adds work on changing-media requests. Different media deliberately no longer share their common text KV prefix; same ordered media still shares it. Long shared-prefix workloads can incur a larger prefill penalty.

Interleaved 100-sample GPU microbench, including host synchronization: 12 MiB raw BLAKE3 **0.099 ms**, typed identity **0.128 ms**, versus old GPU64 **0.100 ms** and D2H+CPU BLAKE3 **3.068 ms**. At 153 MiB, raw BLAKE3 is **0.301 ms** versus old GPU64 **0.237 ms**. This avoids feature-sized D2H, but is not uniformly faster than the old weak GPU hash. Dense hashing needs small scratch buffers; noncontiguous inputs require a contiguous copy. No saturated-throughput claim.

issue.title: [Fix] kernels: Hash tensors over 8 GiB in gpu_tensor_hash

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

`gpu_tensor_hash` computes each tile's offset as `pid * TILE` in int32. For a tensor over 8 GiB (2**31 words), the offset wraps negative and the kernel reads before the buffer: `CUDA error: an illegal memory access`.

`/weights_checker` with `action=checksum` hashes every weight with this kernel, so it crashes the engine on any model with a tensor over 8 GiB per rank. We hit it on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP 8, where each rank's engram table slice is 12.3 GB.

## Modifications

- Compute the offset in int64. Tensors under 8 GiB hash to the same values as before.
- Add a test that hashes a tensor just over 8 GiB (it fails without the fix), and one that pins the hash of a small tensor.

## Accuracy Tests

The change affects hashing only, not model outputs. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (8×B300, TP 8, EP 8), the `/weights_checker` checksum failed before the fix. With the fix, it succeeds in 6.9 s and the engine stays healthy.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hashing a 4 GiB tensor on a B300 takes 2.94 ms before and 2.99 ms after (about 1.7% slower). The kernel isn't on the forward path.

issue.title: [Fix] diffusion: Server warmup reaches every data-parallel replica

labels.name: repo-6e5a3e3c
labels.description: CI: run the baseline test suite on this PR

issue.body:
## Motivation

With `--dp-size > 1`, `--warmup-mode server` warms only one replica. The warmup requests go through `forward`, which routes with the round-robin `_select_replica`, so one warmup request lands on replica 0 only and every other replica serves its first real request cold.

Observed on MiniMax-H3 fl2va, `--num-gpus 2 --dp-size 2 --performance-mode speed --warmup-mode server`: the log shows `Warmup requests 1/1`, and replica 1's first real request took 121.9 s against about 116.6 s warm. Its MP4 also differed from the warm output (video bit-identical, audio SNR 52.8 dB). A 1-GPU server with `--warmup-mode off` reproduces the same cold-first-request output, so that difference is a cold-path effect, not a DP bug; warming every replica removes it from the served traffic.

## Modifications

- `SchedulerClient.forward` / `AsyncSchedulerClient.forward`: new keyword-only `replica` argument that pins an ordinary request to one replica and bypasses `_select_replica`, so `_replica_counter` only advances for real traffic. Control requests still fan out to all replicas.
- `run_async_client_warmup` / `run_sync_client_warmup`: build the warmup list once and send the full list to every endpoint in `server_args.scheduler_endpoints`, replicas in parallel (asyncio tasks / a thread pool) and each replica's list in order. Every replica sees the same list, so `warmup_total` stays correct per replica, and OOM degradation retries independently per replica. All replicas finish before the first error is raised, so a failure does not leave siblings warming in the background of live traffic.
- With `dp_size == 1` behavior is unchanged: the single request still goes to `endpoints[0]` and the counter was never advanced in that case.
- Tests: `test_server_warmup_reaches_every_replica_without_skewing_round_robin` in `test_scheduler_client.py` (sync and async) asserts that with two endpoints both receive the whole warmup list with `warmup_total == 2`, and that real traffic then still starts at replica 0. It fails on `main` and passes here. `test_cfg_parallel_warmup.py` only gains the `scheduler_endpoints` its mock `server_args` now needs.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output change: only which replica receives each warmup request changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured end to end. Unit tests ran on a B300 devbox: `test_scheduler_client`, `test_dp_routing`, `test_cfg_parallel_warmup`, `test_health_warmup_gate`, `test_warmup_probe_degradation`, `test_diffusion_generator_shutdown` and `test_webui` pass together (149 passed, 2 skipped).
